itinerary.title: Cross Agafay desert on the back of a camel and dinner under the stars
body: Experience the mystical charm of Morocco’s desert landscapes without leaving Marrakech on this half-day excursion to the Agafay Desert, located just 45 minutes southeast of the city. Unlike the Sahara, Agafay is a rocky, moon-like desert dotted with sand-dune-like hills, providing a dramatic backdrop for sunset photography and an unforgettable evening in nature.
The Adventure Begins

After pickup from your hotel or riad, your journey takes you along winding roads that descend from the High Atlas foothills into the Agafay Desert. The rugged terrain, scattered with cacti, olive trees, and desert scrub, offers a serene contrast to bustling Marrakech.
Camel Ride & Sunset

Upon arrival, you’ll be greeted with traditional Tuareg robes and scarves, which you can wear for your ride. Mount your camel and traverse the desert’s undulating rocky hills, following trails used by local nomads. Along the way, your guide will lead you to a viewpoint overlooking the horizon, where the sun slowly sets behind the hills, casting golden and pink hues across the landscape. This is the perfect spot for memorable photographs and quiet reflection.
Dinner Under the Stars

After the ride, settle into a cozy, open-air setting for a traditional Moroccan dinner. Enjoy a starter, main course, dessert, and refreshing mint tea while surrounded by the tranquility of the desert under a sky full of stars. The combination of delicious food, peaceful surroundings, and cultural immersion makes this dinner a truly magical experience.
Return to Marrakech
Following your desert adventure, you’ll return to Marrakech in comfort, arriving at your hotel or riad in the evening with memories of a unique desert sunset experience.

summary: This trip combines Atlas Mountain adventure with cultural discovery, making it a perfect choice for travelers who love both biking and authentic encounters.

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Imlil – Biking to Asni
body: Start your biking adventure with a 9:00 AM departure from Marrakech in private transport. Upon arrival in Imlil (1740m), your mountain guide will meet you and get you set for the day. From here, you begin cycling uphill on the asphalt road, climbing gradually toward the Tizi n’Tamatert Pass (2300m), offering breathtaking views of the surrounding Atlas peaks.

After a short break at the pass, continue riding along a scenic track that winds down into the Imnan Valley, dotted with traditional Berber villages such as Ouanskra, Tamguist, Ikiss, and Amsakrou. This ride offers a perfect combination of cultural encounters and natural beauty, as you cycle past terraced fields, walnut orchards, and mud-brick houses.
Around midday, stop in the peaceful village of Arg, where you’ll enjoy a picnic lunch by the river, under the shade of walnut trees — the perfect spot to relax and recharge.

In the afternoon, continue biking through Amsakrou and then descend toward Imsker village, following a road that takes you deeper into the valley landscapes. Finally, you’ll arrive in Asni (1300m), a lively town known for its weekly Berber market every Saturday, where locals gather to trade goods in a colorful, authentic setting.
At the end of the ride, your private transport will be waiting to transfer you comfortably back to Marrakech.

Return to Marrakech by 5:00 PM, completing a full day of adventure, cultural immersion, and breathtaking mountain scenery.

Start your day with breakfast in Marrakech, then depart for Essaouira, a charming seaside town with a rich cultural and historical heritage. The journey passes through scenic landscapes, small roadside towns, and occasional Berber villages.

Essaouira, formerly known as Mogador, has long been a cultural hub, attracting famous musicians like Jimi Hendrix, Bob Marley, and Cat Stevens in the 1960s and 70s. Return to Marrakech in the late afternoon, completing a day filled with culture, history, and coastal beauty.

In recent years a dam was built creating a reservoir which adds to the visual appeal of the valley. Market day is Thursday in Ouirgane.

The most popular activity for visitors is walking – several circuits offer options for people of all abilities, from an hour’s stroll along village tracks, past typical Berber houses, farms and fields, to more challenging walks through the valley and along the river. Your guide will brief you on options when you arrive. Alternatively, enjoy the fresh mountain air and views from a cafe. Lunch is taken in a typical Berber village house, enjoying a home-cooked three course meal of Moroccan salad, couscous with lamb or perhaps a tasty vegetable tagine, fresh seasonal fruits and tea. itinerary.title: Marrakech – Toubkal National Park – Marrakech
body: Escape the bustle of Marrakech and immerse yourself in the majestic scenery of the High Atlas Mountains on this full-day adventure to Toubkal National Park, home to North Africa’s highest peak. This trip offers a perfect combination of nature, culture, and local tradition.
Journey to Imlil

Your day begins with pickup from your hotel or riad in Marrakech at 09:00 AM. Travel in a private vehicle through the winding roads of the Atlas foothills, enjoying scenic mountain views, valleys, and traditional Berber villages along the way. Upon arrival in Imlil, meet your experienced local mountain guide who will lead you through the park.
Hike through Toubkal Valley

The hike begins in the lush Toubkal Valley, passing through green fields adorned with apple, walnut, and cherry trees. As you ascend, the views of Adj Mountain (3,100 m), Aglzim Mountain (3,900 m), and Mount Toubkal (4,167 m) dominate the landscape. The route combines gentle pathways with moderate inclines, offering opportunities to observe traditional mountain life, terraced farms, and local wildlife.
Sidi Chamarouch Shrine

Along the trail, reach Sidi Chamarouch (2,315 m), a small village and holy shrine dedicated to a revered local saint. Pilgrims have visited this site for centuries, and it remains a spiritual and cultural landmark. While non-Muslim visitors cannot cross the bridge into the shrine, you can admire its unique architecture and take photos from outside.
Picnic Lunch

Enjoy a traditional picnic lunch by the river and a waterfall, served on Berber carpets. Your chef prepares fresh Moroccan dishes, allowing you to savor the flavors of the Atlas while surrounded by breathtaking natural scenery. Take your time to relax, explore the area, and capture the tranquil beauty of the surroundings.
Return to Marrakech

After lunch, descend back to Armed Village, enjoying the stunning valley views along the way. Return to Marrakech by private transport in the afternoon, concluding a day filled with adventure, culture, and unforgettable mountain landscapes.

itinerary.title: Free Day in Marrakech
body: Today you leave from El Jadida, you will reach El Oualidia, the pearl of the Atlantic Ocean, this town is a stunningly picturesque little resort – a fishing port and lagoon beach, flanked by a kasbah and a royal villa. The kasbah is seventeenth century, built by the Saadian Sultan El Oualid (after whom the village is named) as a counterweight and alternative to El Jadida, then held by the Portuguese. Until Sultan Sidi Mohammed took El Jadida, the extensive lagoon made an excellent harbour and, as late as 1875, a French geographer thought that “by a little dredging the place would again become the safest shipping station on the whole Moroccan seaboard”. The royal villa, which now stands empty, was built by Mohammed V, who celebrated many birthdays and other family events here. Your afternoon will be devoted to enjoy the beach; a sea food lunch is available to be served at the beach. Your day will end accommodations at the Hotel/raid.
Meals: Breakfast

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Agafay Desert
body: Leave the city behind and head into the Agafay Desert, a dramatic stony landscape stretching to the foothills of the Atlas. Upon arrival, you’ll settle into a luxury camp with sweeping views. Spend the afternoon on a camel trek or try quad biking across the rocky plateaus.
As the sun sets, watch the desert turn golden before enjoying a candlelit dinner under the stars, accompanied by Berber hospitality and music. Overnight in comfortable tents with modern amenities.
Meals: Breakfast, Dinner

itinerary.title: Agafay – High Atlas Mountains (Imlil)
body: Today you’ll climb into the High Atlas Mountains, Morocco’s most scenic range. Stop for a warm Berber family lunch in a traditional home, where you’ll learn about rural mountain life. Later, enjoy a gentle hike around Imlil, walking through terraced fields, walnut groves, and small villages at the foot of Mount Toubkal.
Overnight in a cozy mountain guesthouse or boutique lodge, surrounded by the serenity of the peaks.
Meals: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

itinerary.title: Guided Hike in Toubkal National Park
body: Spend a full day immersed in the fresh mountain air with a guided hike (4–5 hrs, adaptable to your fitness level). Your route passes rushing streams, pine forests, and stone hamlets perched on the hillsides. A picnic lunch will be served in a scenic spot.
Along the way, your guide will share insights into Berber traditions, farming, and mountain ecology. Return to your accommodation in Imlil for dinner and a peaceful night.
Meals: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

itinerary.title: Imlil – Agadir via Tizi n’Test Pass
body: A spectacular drive awaits as you journey across the winding Tizi n’Test Pass (2092m). Pause for breathtaking views over valleys and peaks before visiting the historic Tinmel Mosque, a 12th-century Almohad monument and spiritual birthplace of the dynasty.

Continue descending toward the Atlantic coast to reach Agadir, famous for its crescent beach and relaxed coastal vibe. Spend the evening strolling along the palm-lined promenade or enjoying fresh seafood.
Meals: Breakfast

itinerary.title: Agadir – Essaouira
body: Travel north along Morocco’s Atlantic Coast, passing fishing villages and the unique sight of goats climbing argan trees. Stop at an argan cooperative to learn how the precious oil is produced by local women.
Arrive in Essaouira, a whitewashed port town with Portuguese ramparts, colorful fishing boats, and a bohemian charm beloved by artists and musicians. Check into your riad inside the medina.
Meals: Breakfast

itinerary.title: Exploring Essaouira
body: Discover Essaouira’s treasures on a guided walking tour. Visit the lively harbor, watch fishermen bring in their catch, and stroll the Skala de la Kasbah ramparts with views of the Atlantic. Explore the UNESCO-listed medina, dotted with artisan workshops producing woodcarvings, weaving, and jewelry.
In the afternoon, enjoy free time for shopping or perhaps a camel ride on the beach. In the evening,
Meals: Breakfast

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Home
body: Distance/Time:
- To Marrakech: ~190 km | 3 hrs drive
- To Casablanca: ~370 km | 5.5 hrs drive

After breakfast, drive to your departure city. Depending on your flight, there may be time for last-minute shopping or a café stop along the way. Drop-off at the airport marks the end of your Moroccan journey.

tours.title: 10-Days Morocco Highlights: Cities, Sahara & Atlantic Coast

seo.title: 10-Days Morocco Highlights: Cities, Sahara & Atlantic Coast | Toubkal Peaks Travel Tours

itinerary.title: Arrival in Casablanca – Transfer to Rabat
body: Welcome to Morocco! Upon arrival at Casablanca airport, your driver will meet you and give you a warm introduction to your journey ahead. Depending on your flight schedule, you may visit the Hassan II Mosque, one of the largest mosques in the world and a true masterpiece of Moroccan craftsmanship. Built partly on land and partly over the Atlantic Ocean, its towering minaret rises 210 meters into the sky, guiding worshippers with a laser beam directed toward Mecca.

After your visit, continue to Rabat, Morocco’s laid-back capital city and home of the Royal Palace, Andalusian gardens, and the medieval Oudaya Kasbah overlooking the Atlantic. Dinner and overnight in a traditional Moroccan-style hotel.

itinerary.title: Rabat – Meknes – Volubilis – Fes
body: After breakfast, start your day with a brief exploration of Rabat before heading inland. Your first stop is the ancient Roman ruins of Volubilis, a UNESCO World Heritage Site dating back to the 3rd century BC. Here you’ll wander through remarkably preserved mosaics, basilicas, and triumphal arches that reflect the glory of the Roman Empire in North Africa.

Next, drive to Meknes, once the capital of Sultan Moulay Ismail in the 17th century. Visit the monumental Bab Mansour Gate, considered one of the most beautiful gates in Morocco, and the granaries of Sahrij Souani. After lunch in a local restaurant, continue towards Fes, the spiritual heart of Morocco. Overnight stay in a traditional riad.

itinerary.title: Full Day in Fes – Guided City Tour
body: Step back in time as you explore the cultural capital of Morocco. Accompanied by a local expert guide, discover Fes el-Bali, the largest and oldest medina in the world, a labyrinth of over 9,000 narrow streets and alleys.
Highlights include:
- The Royal Palace Gate and the old Jewish quarter (Mellah)
- The Bou Inania Madrasa, a stunning example of Marinid architecture
- The University of Al Quaraouiyine, the oldest continuously operating university in the world, founded by Fatima al-Fihri
- The colorful tanneries, where leather is dyed in giant stone vats
- The Najjarine Fountain and the woodworkers’ souk

After a traditional Moroccan lunch inside the medina, enjoy a panoramic view of the city from the old fortress and visit a pottery cooperative. Evening free to rest or explore the lively streets of Fes at your own pace. Overnight in riad.

itinerary.title: Fes – Ifrane – Midelt – Ziz Valley – Merzouga
body: A scenic adventure awaits! Depart Fes and head south through the Middle Atlas Mountains, stopping at Ifrane, often nicknamed the “Switzerland of Morocco” for its alpine-style architecture. Continue to the cedar forests of Azrou, home to playful Barbary macaques.

Your journey then winds through mountain passes, Berber villages, and the Ziz Valley, famous for its palm groves and dramatic landscapes. After crossing into the desert region, you’ll arrive in Merzouga, gateway to the spectacular Erg Chebbi dunes. Overnight in a desert riad or kasbah with dinner.

itinerary.title: Exploring Merzouga & Sahara Desert Camel Trek
body: After breakfast, explore the desert region and learn about its unique culture. Visit the Gnawa people in Khamlia village and enjoy their traditional music. Depending on the season, you may also see the seasonal Merzouga lake, home to migratory birds such as flamingos.

In the afternoon, prepare for a camel trek into the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi. Your camel caravan will carry you through the rolling sands just in time to witness a magical desert sunset. Arrive at your luxury desert camp, where a traditional Moroccan dinner is served under the starry Saharan sky. Spend the night in a Bedouin-style tent surrounded by silence and starlight.

itinerary.title: Merzouga – Todra Gorge – Dades Valley – Ouarzazate – Ait Ben Haddou
body: Wake up early to watch the breathtaking sunrise over the dunes, then ride camels back to the village where your driver awaits. Today’s route takes you through spectacular landscapes, beginning with the Todra Gorge, a dramatic canyon carved by the Todra River with cliffs towering over 300 meters.

Continue along the Road of a Thousand Kasbahs, through fertile valleys and fortified villages. Stop at Ouarzazate, often called the “Hollywood of Africa” due to its famous film studios. Finally, arrive at the UNESCO World Heritage site of Ait Ben Haddou, Morocco’s most iconic ksar (fortified village), used as a backdrop for movies such as Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Overnight in a traditional kasbah hotel.

itinerary.title: Ait Ben Haddou – High Atlas – Essaouira
body: After breakfast, depart Ait Ben Haddou and cross the High Atlas Mountains via the scenic Tizi n’Tichka pass (2260m). Along the way, stop at a women’s cooperative to see how argan oil is traditionally produced.

By late afternoon, arrive in Essaouira, Morocco’s most charming coastal city. With its whitewashed medina, Portuguese fortifications, and relaxed seaside atmosphere, Essaouira is a refreshing contrast to the desert and mountains. Stroll along the ramparts at sunset and soak up the Atlantic breeze. Overnight in a boutique riad.

itinerary.title: Essaouira – Marrakech
body: Enjoy a relaxed morning in Essaouira. Visit the vibrant fishing port, explore the medina’s artisan workshops, or simply relax on the beach. Later, drive inland towards the “Red City” of Marrakech, arriving by the afternoon. The rest of the day is free for you to rest or explore the bustling square of Jemaa el-Fnaa, where snake charmers, storytellers, and food stalls bring the city to life. Overnight in a traditional riad.

itinerary.title: Full Day in Marrakech – Guided City Tour
body: Today, discover the vibrant sights and sounds of Marrakech, Morocco’s most famous city. Your private guide will lead you through the medina’s labyrinth of souks, filled with colorful spices, textiles, and handicrafts.
Highlights include:
- The Koutoubia Mosque with its iconic minaret
- The Saadian Tombs, resting place of the Saadian dynasty
- The Bahia Palace, a masterpiece of Moroccan architecture
- The lush Majorelle Gardens, once owned by Yves Saint Laurent
- The lively square of Jemaa el-Fnaa, with its street performers and food stalls
In the evening, you may choose to enjoy a traditional Moroccan dinner with live music and dance. Overnight in riad.

itinerary.title: Departure from Marrakech (or Casablanca)
body: Your Moroccan adventure comes to an end today. After breakfast, enjoy free time until your airport transfer. Depending on your flight, you may depart from Marrakech airport or drive back to Casablanca airport (additional cost).
We wish you a safe journey home and hope Morocco has left you with unforgettable memories of its warm people, vibrant culture, and breathtaking landscapes.

body: Spend a full day exploring Fes, the spiritual and cultural heart of Morocco. Highlights include the Medersa Bou Inania, Qaraouine Mosque, the labyrinthine medina, and bustling souks. Learn about traditional crafts and Moroccan architecture. Walking distance: 4–5 km with breaks.

itinerary.title: arrived in Marrakech Airport
body: Day1: arrived in Marrakech Airport, and transfer to the hotel/raid

itinerary.title: Marrakesh – Essaouira
body: Departure at 9 o’clock in the morning when the driver will come to fetch you from whichever riad or hotel you might be staying in. You will take the motor-way, passing thousands of Morocco-specific argane trees on the way to this blue and white, very individual, sea-side town and port. Essaouira is many tourists’ darling! Previously known as Mogador to the Portuguese inhabitants, it is a charming place, well- known for local handicrafts, especially thuja wood furniture, carving and small artefacts, sold in innumerable shops along the windy streets. At the sea front, the customer chooses a selection of freshly caught fish to have prepared on the spot. Essaouira has a favourable micro-climate; mild in winter and cool in summer, although frequently windy, which makes it very popular among surfers.

itinerary.title: Essaouira – Sidi Ifni
body: Leaving Essaouira after breakfast, you follow the coastal road south with constant views of the Atlantic, often battering the rocks and sending up picturesque spray as it beats against the rocks. We pass Agadir and continue south to Tiznit, the town famous for its silver jewelry. From here we turn towards the sea and take the particularly beautiful coastal road to Sid Ifni. This is a little neat blue and white town with a distinctly Spanish feel to it. It takes its name from a local holy man and was the capital of the Ait Ba’arame tribe famous for its resistance against the Spanish.

itinerary.title: Sidi Ifni – Tafraoute
body: From Sidi Ifni we turn north again back to Tiznit, where we stop to wander the soukhs. From here we enter the Anti Atlas mountains, passing Tighmi and the Kerdous pass, then Tizourhane until we reach Tafraoute. This road is one of the most beautiful roads in the Moroccan mountains.

itinerary.title: Tafraoute – Taroudant
body: After breakfast we visit the famous painted rocks, colored in 1984 by the Belgian artist, Jean Verame. He used 18 tons of blue, pink, red, and black paint, helped in his project by men from the Tafraoute fire-brigade. This work of art has proved very controversial; people choosing to wonder at it, question its existence and to despise it. It is certainly an individual and “other” piece of art. We then set out northwards continuing to follow the spectacular road which the Ait Baha river to the town of the same name. Later we turn right towards Taroudant, “the little Marrakesh”, so called for the similarity of its ramparts and town walls to those of the “red city”. Here we spend the night having explored the town.

itinerary.title: Tafraoute – Chagaga
body: After breakfast we continue towards the desert. We cross the two passes of Tizi-n-Tighatine and Tizi-n-Ikhsane before reaching Kourkouda and Taznakht . This small town is famous for its Berber kelims and carpets, lunch in Foum-Zguid. From here we continue south and drive into the Sahara across the stony desert, “reg” and across the now dried-up Lake Iriqui. In the middle of this lake we can search for fossils. And arriv Chagaga dunes here you take a camel ride and can clamber up to the top of the high dunes to watch the sunset. At the foot of the dunes, we have dinner and spend the night in a camp of nomad tents.

itinerary.title: Chagaga – Ouarzazate
body: After breakfast in the desert camp, the itinerary crosses another 60 km of desert road via the Sacred Oasis to arrive in M’hamid You continue to north up the Draa Valley towards Zagora for lunch. This small town is the largest oasis in the Draa Valley and is particularly famous for its dates. From here we follow the ancient caravan route used by the caravans that had crossed the Sahara for days and weeks bringing treasures from Mali or Mauretania. The road passes between the river and the mountains past all the Kasbahs and the local gardens giving you a clearer impression of life here in this area of Morocco. In Agdez at the head of the Draa Valley, you can stop to visit the oldest and most famous kasbah in the valley, Kasbah Tamnougalte. It is still partly inhabited by about eleven families. You then continue to Ouarzazate crossing the Tizi-n-Tififte pass, where some scenes from the film “Babel” were shot. In Ouarzazate you stay in Hotel/Riad.

itinerary.title: Ouarzazate – Marrakesh
body: After breakfast, driving north from Ouarzazate, you leave the main road and take a side road to Ait ben Haddou, which also belonged to the Lords of the Atlas, the Glaoui family. This is the most famous Kasbah in Morocco and a UNESCO World Heritage site. It is also well-known as being the backdrop to many Hollywood blockbusters, such as “Alexander”, “the Gladiator”, “the Kingdom of Heaven” The road then continues along the Ounila valley with beautiful and prosperous villages, stunning mountains and views to Telouet, where you will stop to visit the Kasbah and perhaps have lunch. We reach Marrakesh by the early evening.

body: This morning from Marrakech, your Mountain guide and private vehicle will meet you at the hotel/riad at 09:00 in the morning to start the journey for 1h,30munte, and then Your hike will first go up to the Tirst Plateau and down to Ouirgane forest, full of junipers and pine trees. Following, you will continue to L’khmis Village, the village of Torourd , and then up through the Azaden Valley with very nice views of Takhrkhourt (large forest) in Toubkal National Park . Then, it is on to the Tasa Ouirgane with a small village. Here, we will have lunch in a local Berber family’s home and finally head back a different route to the Marirgha and travel back to Marrakech. The total walking time will be five hrs.

itinerary.title: Arrive in Tangier Airport/Ferry – Transfer to Hotel/Riad
body: Transport, Breakfast

You’ll tart Tangier Morocco tours via Sahara desert, by picking you up from tangier airport or Ferry you are and transfer you to your hotel/riad to relax and store your luggage. Then in the afternoon you can take a tour around tangier to discover Spartel cape and the hercules caves by your private transport. From the Greek hero Hercules caves you’ll have an exceptional view of the strait -of- Gibraltar and the Atlantic- Ocean. Then you can visit the Kasbah a magnificent Minaret,” . At the end of your tour, your driver will take you back to your Hotel/riad for (overnight stay) .

itinerary.title: Tangier – Chefchaouen Blue City
body: Transport (2hrs), Breakfast

This morning after breakfast at your hotel/riad your driver will pick you up to start your Morocco adventure desert tours, towards Chefchaouen, the blue and white City Established in 1471 by Moulay Ali Ben Moussa Ben Rached El Alamiand Up on arrival to Chefchaouen, we’ll drop you off to your hotel/riad to relax and store your luggage. After that you can take a tour around Chefchaouen to discover the best monuments such as kasbah built back to 18th century, central mosque, local market (souk) full of tourists souvenirs,cafes with Moroccan original style menus. Chefchaouen Medina is small and easy to explore by yourself.

itinerary.title: Chefchaouen – Volubilis – Meknes – Fez
body: Transport (4hrs), Breakfast

Leave Chefchaouen and head south to Volubilis, the most important and extensive remains of a Roman city in Morocco, and one of the most distant of the Empire’s domain, thanks to the powerful Berber tribes who showed themselves to be more than a match for the conquering legionnaires. Once one of the most important regions producing grain to feed the voracious Roman appetite, and wild animals to keep the crowds entertained as they tried to devour gladiators in the arena, this prosperous provincial city was home to some 200,000 residents at the height of its glory, with sumptuous mosaics still to be seen in some of the most luxurious homes.

You move on to Moulay Idriss, which, from a distance, looks like a sitting camel. The oldest town in Morocco, it was founded by Moulay Idriss I in 789, having fled Mecca because of religious and tribal conflicts. It was here that the Idrisid dynasty was founded, and the town has the only round minaret in Morocco. You end today in one of Morocco’s four imperial cities, Fez.

itinerary.title: Fez Guided Tour
body: Transport, Breakfast

Your own private Fez guide tour, Your tour lasts from 9:30am until 4:30pm with a break for lunch. Before you head out in the morning, you can discuss with your guide which sights you’d like to see most. If you have never been to Fez before you might like to read our travel guide to Fes, which will not only give you a fascinating insight into this equally fascinating city, but will also help you decide which sites you would like to experience with the help of your guide. It really will be worth your while to put yourself in his hands and allow him to show you the mysteries and secrets of the nine thousand streets and alleyways that make up this amazing historic city – but don’t worry, you won’t be expected to walk all of them!

itinerary.title: Fez – Ifrane – Ziz Valley – Erfoud – Merzouga
body: Transport, Breakfast , Dinner

Today you will head towards Midelt passing through Ifrane. Located in the mountains of the Middle Atlas, this is an oasis of coolness and vegetation. With its lakes and fountains of alpine characteristics known throughout the world as the “Moroccan Switzerland”, Above all for the European style houses with sloping roofs which have nothing to do with the traditional architecture of Morocco. Then, we will drive through “Azrou ” an important Berber village located in the interior of the Middle Atlas and surrounded by hills. The main interest of this small town is its surrounding cedar forest and where you can see the famous Big Gouraud Cedar the largest millennial of the region, you’ll heading though the lash palm groves Ziz valley and the date palm city Erfoud. In the first place, one of the charms of this town is its tranquility. We will also have the possibility to visit the factory of fossils. Then, we will continue to the Sahara desert Merzouga , overnight at the Hotel/Riad

itinerary.title: Merzouga – Erg Chebbi Sand dunes , night under the stars
body: Transport, Breakfast, Dinner

Today you are going to experience one of the most memorable moments of your Morocco adventure as you make your way into the dunes of Morocco’s Erg Chebbi region of the Sahara Desert. You’ll have this morning to relax and/or explore Merzouga ; Khamlia and desert lake, also you can have a desert pizza at one of the best traditional desert restaurant before preparing for a memorable night under the stars. A hour’s camel ride weaving along the tops of the sand dunes brings you to your camp, with its Bedouin style tents and thick Moroccan carpets to keep the sand from between your toes. A tasty meal is your dinner, eaten by candlelight. You’ll probably choose to drift off to sleep while watching the twinkling stars during the Summer time.

itinerary.title: Sahara Desert – Tinjdad – Todra Gorge – Dades Gorge
body: Transport, Breakfast , Dinner

This morning, your camel man will wake you up to see another beautiful sunrise which will maybe be the best one you see in your life. After the sunrise, you will mount your camel going back to your hotel before you leave to Rissani, Tinghir, and the amazing Todra Gorges (the highest and narrowest Gorges in Morocco). There, we will stop for lunch in Tinjdad ksar Elkhorbat (optional). Explore the Dades Valley in this unique Tangier Morocco tours via Sahara desert, where you will see the magical sand castles and the amazing rock formations known as monkey toes. Overnight accommodation will be in a Hotel/Riad/Kasbah in Dades valley .

itinerary.title: Dades Gorge – Ouarzazate – Ait Ben Haddou
body: Transport, Breakfast , Dinner

After your breakfast in your hotel, you will travel through the Dades Valley towards Kalaa M’gouna and Ouarzazate. Then you will travel toward Ouarzazate via Skoura the Valley of 1,000 Kasbahs From there you will continue passing several Kasbahs toward El Kalaa Mgouna which is known for vast fields of pink roses that are used in perfume. Many small shops selling rose products such as rose water and rose-scented soap. Then, you will continue to Ouarzazate known as the Hollywood of Morocco, and visit the Film studios and then to Ait ben Haddou , overnight at the hotel/Kasbah .

itinerary.title: Ait Ben Haddou – Telouet – Marrakech
body: Transport, Breakfast

Your most vivid memory from today will be of your visit to Ait Ben Haddou, a UNESCO world heritage site, which, as well as being the best extant example in the area of a walled town protected by Kasbahs, the homes of the wealthy and powerful, has been the backdrop to many Hollywood blockbusters and major historical television programs, including Gladiator and Lawrence of Arabia. If you are a fan of A Game of Thrones you will recognize Ait Ben Haddou from the final scene of series three. (The series has used a number of locations around Morocco.) From Ait Ben Haddou, you may wish to continue to the lesser-visited (and possibly more impressive) area of Telouet. Here, you can meander about the former palace of the Glaoui family and even enjoy lunch with a private local (once celebrity) Berber singer chanting of days gone by. The last leg of today’s journey is over the High Atlas Mountains on the impressive zig-zag of Tiz n Tichka pass, eventually to arrive in Marrakech for the overnight.

itinerary.title: Marrakech Guided Tour
body: Transport, Breakfast

Exploring Marrakech with an official guide, the tour lasts from 9:30am till 5pm, The First thing you will see is the historic Koutoubia Mosque from 12century, known for its four distinct faces. Moreover, the Saadian tombs and Bahia palace which showcases the finest examples of traditional design elements. Such as decorative tile, painted, wood, carved plaster, and calligraphy. Furthermore, you will have the chance to visit the beautiful Majorelle Gardens just outside the ancient medina. Where the famous French stylist Yves Saint Laurent is buried, trees and flowers from the 5 continents gathered together in an amazing oasis of peace it’s really worth to be seen. Then, visit the souks and end your day in Jama’a el-Fna square, which is a UNESCO world heritage site, In Jama’a el-Fna you will see snake charmers, story-tellers, henna artists and dancers. This square has been the heart of the Medina since the 12th century. A home for performers, travelers and fortune-tellers, Stop for a glass of fresh squeezed orange juice and enjoy the carnival atmosphere. If you’re feeling brave, have a bowl of fresh snails or some sheep’s head or have dinner at your hotel or riad. Finally, overnight will be in a hotel or riad/Marrakech

itinerary.title: Arrival in Casablanca → Rabat
body: Arrive in Casablanca, visit the magnificent Hassan II Mosque, one of the largest in the world, beautifully set on the Atlantic Ocean. Continue to Rabat, Morocco’s elegant capital.
Highlights: Hassan II Mosque • Corniche • Hassan Tower • Kasbah of the Udayas
Overnight in Rabat.

itinerary.title: Rabat → Chefchaouen
body: Explore Rabat’s major sites including the Royal Palace, Mausoleum of Mohammed V, and Kasbah des Oudayas before heading north through rolling hills to the charming Blue City of Chefchaouen nestled in the Rif Mountains.
Overnight in Chefchaouen.

itinerary.title: Explore Chefchaouen or Akchour Waterfalls (Optional)
body: Enjoy a relaxed morning exploring Chefchaouen’s blue-washed streets, colorful doors, and local markets.
Optional Excursion: Short hike (1–4 hrs) to Akchour Waterfalls, a lush green valley perfect for a picnic or swim.
Overnight in Chefchaouen.

itinerary.title: Chefchaouen → Volubilis → Moulay Idriss → Meknes → Fes
body: Head south to explore the Roman ruins of Volubilis, Morocco’s best-preserved archaeological site. Visit the holy town of Moulay Idriss Zerhoun and the imperial city of Meknes before continuing to Fes.
Highlights: Volubilis • Moulay Idriss • Bab Mansour Gate • Meknes Medina
Overnight in Fes.

itinerary.title: Fes Guided Visit
body: Explore the spiritual and cultural heart of Morocco!

After breakfast, meet your local Fes guide for a full-day walking and driving tour through Fes el-Bali, the ancient walled medina and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Step back in time as you wander through narrow labyrinthine alleys, centuries-old madrasas, mosques, and artisan workshops that preserve traditions passed down for generations.
Highlights of the Day:
- The Royal Palace (Dar el Makhzen): Admire the majestic golden gates surrounded by intricate zellij tilework.
- Mellah (Jewish Quarter): Discover the history of the Jewish community and see the 17th-century Ibn Danan Synagogue.
- Bou Inania Madrasa: A masterpiece of Marinid architecture, famous for its detailed wood carvings and stucco.
- Tanneries of Chouara: Watch traditional leather-making methods from a rooftop terrace overlooking the colorful dye pits — a must-see sight!
- Al-Qarawiyyin University and Mosque: Founded in 859 AD, this is the oldest continually operating university in the world.
- Souks and Artisan Quarters: Explore workshops where artisans craft copperware, ceramics, textiles, and jewelry using age-old techniques.
- Borj Nord Viewpoint: For a panoramic view of Fes Medina and its surrounding hills — perfect for photos!
Lunch Suggestion:
Enjoy a traditional Moroccan meal in a local riad restaurant — try dishes like chicken tagine with preserved lemons, or couscous with caramelized onions and raisins.
Afternoon Options (Optional Add-ons):
- Visit the Dar Batha Museum, showcasing Moroccan arts and crafts.
- Explore the modern city of Fes el-Jdid for a contrast between old and new.
Overnight in Fes at a traditional riad within the medina.

itinerary.title: Fes → Ifrane → Midelt → Erfoud → Merzouga (Desert Gate)
body: After an early breakfast, depart Fes around 7:00 AM for a scenic journey toward the Sahara Desert. Travel through the ever-changing landscapes of the Middle Atlas Mountains, passing through charming towns, lush valleys, and dramatic plateaus.
Highlights along the way:
- Ifrane – “The Little Switzerland of Morocco”
A charming alpine-style town known for its clean streets, flower gardens, and European architecture.
- Azrou Cedar Forest
Stop to see the famous Barbary macaque monkeys in the cedar forest — a fun moment for nature and wildlife lovers.
- Middle Atlas & Ziz Valley
Continue past Midelt, nestled between the Middle and High Atlas, and descend through the Ziz Gorge, a dramatic canyon leading to the fertile Ziz Valley, lined with date palms and ancient kasbahs.
- Erfoud & Merzouga Dunes
As you reach the edge of the desert, the scenery transforms into golden sands and vast open plains — your first glimpse of the Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga.
Arrive in Merzouga by late afternoon, where your camel caravan awaits. Ride across the dunes at sunset to reach your luxury desert camp, nestled among the towering sands.
Evening Experience:
Enjoy a traditional Berber dinner under a starlit sky, followed by live drumming and storytelling around the campfire — an unforgettable night in the Sahara.

itinerary.title: Merzouga Desert → Todra Gorge → Dades Valley
itinerary.accommodation: Boutique Kasbah or Guesthouse in Dades or Skoura
body: Wake up early to witness one of Morocco’s most unforgettable sights — the sunrise over the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi. The first rays of light paint the sand in glowing shades of amber and gold, offering the perfect photo moment.

After breakfast, enjoy a camel trek back across the dunes, Continue your journey north through Erfoud, famous for its date market and fossil workshops, then pass through Tinejdad, where you can visit the Berber Museum of Culture to gain insight into local traditions and desert heritage.

Soon, you’ll arrive at the majestic Todra Gorge (Tinghir region) — a natural wonder carved by the Todra River through towering limestone cliffs that rise up to 300 meters high. Enjoy time to walk along the gorge floor, where locals tend small gardens and rock climbers challenge the sheer canyon walls.

After lunch at the gorge, the route winds west toward the Dades Valley, often called the “Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs.” Here, the scenery transforms into spectacular red and ochre rock formations, including the famous “Monkey Fingers” cliffs and dramatic switchback roads leading up the valley.
Arrive by late afternoon and settle into a cozy guesthouse or kasbah-style hotel surrounded by palm groves and ancient fortified villages.
Evening Experience:
Relax on the terrace with panoramic views of the Dades Gorge, enjoy a homemade dinner, and experience the warm Berber hospitality of the valley.

itinerary.title: Dades Valley → Ouarzazate → Aït Ben Haddou → Imlil (High Atlas)
body: After breakfast, depart from the Dades Valley and follow the scenic road toward Kelaat M’Gouna, also known as the Valley of Roses . This charming area is famous for its spring rose festival and for producing delicate rosewater and essential oils. You may stop at a local cooperative to see how these traditional products are made by Berber women using time-honored techniques.

Continue your drive through the Skoura Oasis , a lush valley of palm groves and ancient kasbahs (fortified homes), including the well-preserved Kasbah Amridil, one of the most beautiful and iconic kasbahs in southern Morocco. The landscapes gradually change from fertile valley floors to the arid, cinematic plains surrounding Ouarzazate , often called the “Hollywood of Africa.”

Here, you can visit the world-famous Atlas Film Studios, where international movies and series like Gladiator, The Mummy, and Game of Thrones were filmed. A guided visit reveals the impressive sets, props, and stories behind Morocco’s thriving film industry.

Just a short drive further west brings you to the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Aït Ben Haddou , a striking example of southern Moroccan earthen clay architecture. This ancient ksar (fortified village), perched on a hill along the old caravan route between the Sahara and Marrakech, has been featured in numerous films and remains one of Morocco’s most photogenic sites. Stroll through its narrow alleys and climb to the top for breathtaking panoramic views over the desert plain and the snow-capped Atlas Mountains.

After lunch overlooking the kasbah, the journey continues over the dramatic Tizi n’Tichka Pass (2,260 m) , the highest road pass in Morocco. Enjoy sweeping views of mountain valleys, Berber hamlets clinging to terraced slopes, and the ever-changing colors of the High Atlas.

By late afternoon, descend into the serene Imlil Valley , nestled at the foot of Mount Toubkal (4,167 m) — North Africa’s highest peak. The air becomes cooler and fresher as you reach this charming mountain village, surrounded by walnut groves, terraced fields, and traditional stone houses.
Evening Experience:
Settle into a cozy riad or mountain lodge. Enjoy a home-cooked Berber dinner and the tranquil ambiance of the High Atlas, where the only sounds are the river and distant mule bells.

itinerary.title: Imlil: Berber Villages Hike & Traditional Lunch
body: Wake up to the fresh mountain air and the sound of birds echoing across the valley. After breakfast at your riad, set off on a gentle hike through the scenic Imlil Valley (1,740 m) — the gateway to Mount Toubkal. Your local mountain guide will lead you along ancient mule trails that connect the Berber villages scattered across the slopes of the High Atlas.

The walk passes through terraced fields, apple and walnut groves, and crystal-clear mountain streams, where villagers still draw water using traditional irrigation channels. Along the way, you’ll visit picturesque hamlets such as Aroumd, Tamatert, or Armed, where stone-built houses blend naturally into the surrounding mountainsides.

Enjoy frequent stops for photos and for meeting friendly locals going about their daily lives — women baking bread in clay ovens, children playing by the water channels, and farmers tending to their mules or small orchards.

Around midday, you’ll be warmly welcomed into a Berber family home for a freshly prepared traditional lunch — often featuring tajine, homemade bread, olive oil, and mint tea. It’s a wonderful opportunity to experience authentic mountain hospitality and learn about Berber customs, traditions, and daily routines in this remote yet welcoming region.

After lunch, enjoy a leisurely walk back down to your riad or guesthouse, where the rest of the afternoon is free to relax — perhaps on the terrace overlooking the snow-capped peaks or with a cup of Moroccan tea as the sun sets over the valley.
Evening Experience:
Enjoy a cozy dinner prepared with local ingredients and spend a peaceful night under the stars of the High Atlas.

itinerary.title: Imlil → Marrakech
body: After breakfast, say goodbye to the peaceful mountains and the friendly faces of Imlil as you begin your journey back to the vibrant city of Marrakech. The drive winds gently down through the Aït Mizane Valley, offering spectacular views of terraced fields, walnut trees, and snow-capped peaks in the distance.

Pass through Asni, a lively market town where locals from nearby villages gather to trade fresh produce, livestock, and handmade goods. If it’s a Saturday, you may even catch the weekly souk — a colorful scene filled with the aromas of spices, fresh mint, and grilled corn.

Continue descending into the Haouz Plain, where the landscape gradually shifts from rugged mountain terrain to open farmland dotted with olive groves and adobe villages. As the red walls of Marrakech come into view, you’ll feel the contrast between the calm of the High Atlas and the bustling rhythm of the “Red City.”

Upon arrival in Marrakech, check into your riad or hotel, ideally located within or near the Medina — the city’s historic heart. The rest of the day is yours to relax or begin exploring the city’s rich heritage:
- Enjoy a rooftop dinner overlooking Jemaa el-Fna Square, where storytellers, musicians, and food stalls bring the night to life.
Evening Suggestion:
Treat yourself to a traditional hammam (Moroccan spa) or a dinner show with live music and belly dancing for a memorable evening back in the city.

itinerary.title: Marrakech Guided Visit
body: Start your day with a guided exploration of Marrakech, Morocco’s most captivating imperial city — a perfect blend of history, culture, and vibrant energy.

Begin at the Majorelle Garden, an oasis of exotic plants and cobalt-blue art once owned by Yves Saint Laurent. Continue to the Koutoubia Mosque, Marrakech’s iconic landmark, and the Bahia Palace, a masterpiece of Moroccan-Andalusian architecture filled with intricate mosaics and carved ceilings.

Stroll through the narrow lanes of the Medina, a UNESCO World Heritage site, where you’ll discover colorful souks brimming with spices, textiles, lanterns, and leather goods. Visit Ben Youssef Madrasa, an ancient Islamic school famed for its stunning craftsmanship (optional visit depending on time).

In the afternoon, experience the magic of Jemaa el-Fna Square, the beating heart of Marrakech. Here, snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and food stalls bring the square to life as the sun sets over the city.
Overnight in Marrakech.

itinerary.title: Departure from Marrakech or Casablanca
body: After breakfast, enjoy some free time to relax or explore Marrakech at your own pace — perhaps do some last-minute shopping in the souks or unwind at a traditional hammam.
At the scheduled time, your driver will transfer you to Marrakech Menara Airport for your departure flight.
If your flight departs from Casablanca, you’ll travel via the highway (approx. 2.5–3 hrs drive).
Your unforgettable 12-day Moroccan adventure comes to an end — filled with the colors, flavors, and warm hospitality of Morocco.
Thank you for traveling with Toubkal Peaks Travel!

itinerary.title: Casablanca – Rabat
body: Transport (1,5hrs), Breakfast, Driving distance: 100km

Welcome to Morocco! Upon arrival at the airport, you will be met by our local representative. Upon arrival to the airport in Casablanca, be welcomed and assisted through customs & immigrations before being transferred to Rabat. En route you will visit the impressive Hassan II Mosque, the second largest mosque in the world after Mecca in Saudi Arabia (direct payment for the entrance). Continue to visit the Museum of Moroccan Judaism in Casablanca, that museum, which covers an area of 700 square meters, is the first of its kind in the Arab world. It consists of created by the Jewish Community of Casablanca in 1997 with the support of the Foundation of Jewish-Moroccan Cultural Heritage. It uses world-class standards of conservation for its national and international collections. Drive to Rabat and continue on to Sale, the twin city of Rabat and the birthplace of Rabbi Hayyim Ben Moses Attar, the famous 18th century scholar and cabbalist, known throughout the Jewish world for his bible commentary, the “Or Ha-Hayyim”, the famous rabbi, Raphael Encaoua is buried in the Sale cemetery, before being transferred to the hotel.
Accommodation at: Traditional Moroccan style Hotel (Standard).

itinerary.title: Rabat – Tangier
body: Transport (3hrs), Breakfast, Driving distance: 240km

Travel today between Rabat and Tangier in a private vehicle with an English speaking driver, stopping en-route for some touring around the diplomatic and administrative capital of Morocco, Rabat. Visit the Royal Palace, the wild gardens of the Chellah, a 14th-century Merinid necropolis and a walk through the Andalusian Gardens, within the walls of the Kasbah of the Oudaya. Visit the Hassan Tower, a huge unfinished minaret, built mostly at the end of the 12th century, an architectural wonder worth seeing. Upon arrival into Tangier a transfer to hotel is provided.

Enjoy a city tour of Tangier and its surroundings, including the Spartel Cape and the Hercules Caves. Marvel at the picturesque views of the Atlantic Ocean and the famed Strait of Gibraltar, a perfect photo opportunity. Mingle through the Kasbah district located next to the port, before heading towards the old Medina. Visit some of the many shops that line the streets of the Medina and find the perfect handicraft, gift, or memory for yourself or your loved ones. Pass the Grand Sacco and the Mendoubia Park believed to contain the fossil remains of some truly ancient creatures, including some Dragon bones. Next, visit the Petit Sacco with its multitudes of boutique hotels and riads. This historically location has hosted a variety of famous artists including Matisse, Camille Saint Saens, Paul Bowles.
Accommodation at: Traditional Moroccan style Hotel (Standard).

itinerary.title: Tangier – Chefchaouen
body: Transport (5hrs), Breakfast, Driving distance: 261km

Travel today between Tangier and Chefchaouen by private vehicle and English speaking driver. Travel in a privately driven vehicle to explore the city of Chefchaouen. This beautiful city is located on the Rift of the mountainous region between the Mediterranean Sea and the Iberian Peninsula. Chefchaouen is known worldwide for its Medina of shady alleys, whitewashed houses with blue turquoise doors, wrought iron windows and colorful tile covered roofs. The souks are decorated with their traditionally dressed inhabitants boasting their straw hats, Overnight in Chefchaouen.
Accommodation at: Traditional Moroccan style Hotel (Standard).

itinerary.title: Chefchaouen – Fes
body: Transport (5hrs), Breakfast, Driving distance: 261km

A private vehicle with English speaking driver will provide a transfer between Chefchaouen and Fes. During the transfer, enjoy some brief touring stops including a visit to Meknes, the famed Ismailia capital known for its 40 km long walls and numerous gates. Next, visit Bab Mansour, the Royal stables, the amazing markets and also the popular Jewish quarter. Before arriving in Fes, explore the ruins of the ancient city of Volubilis and the holy city of Moulay Idriss. Upon arrival into Fes, a hotel drop-off is provided.
Accommodation at: Traditional Moroccan style Hotel (Standard).

itinerary.title: Fes Guided Visit
body: Transport , Breakfast, English speaking Local Guide
A private vehicle with English speaking city tour guide and driver will be at your disposal for the day.

Explore the cultural and spiritual center of Morocco during this full day tour of Fes. Also known as Fes el Bali, this UNESCO World Heritage Site was founded in the 9th century, and is home to the world’s oldest university. The city of Fes reached its true economic and cultural height in the 13th–14th centuries under the Merinids, when it replaced Marrakech as the capital of the kingdom. Although the political capital of Morocco was transferred to Rabat in 1912, Fes has retained its status as the country’s Artisan centre. Artisan workshops in the medina are as active today as they were 100 years ago, and strongly contribute to the city’s industrial economy. Trades such as blacksmithing, leather working, ceramics, silk, tapestries, and sculpting are still practiced in these workshops today. The original ramparts still protect this ancient city and its estimated 9000 narrow passageways and bustling streets.
Accommodation at: Traditional Moroccan style Hotel (Standard).

itinerary.title: Fes – Erfoud – Merzouga
body: Transport (7hrs), Breakfast, Dinner, Driving distance: 480km

Sit back and relax as a privately driven vehicle, with English speaking driver, provides you with a transfer between Fes and Erfoud. En-route you’ll pass through a scenic forest of cedars and across the Middle Atlas Mountain range to the mineral mining city of Midelt, where a stop for lunch is scheduled. This journey continues along through the dramatic Ziz Gorge, passing en-route the ancient, holy city of Rissani. It is here where the one would find the ruins of Sijilmasa, a once capital and merchant stopping locale for the ancient caravan routings of the 8th century. After an approximate 7 hours of travel you will arrive at your final destination of Erfoud.
Enjoy a traditional Moroccan lunch at the hotel Taddarte in Midelt.

A 4×4 vehicle will be waiting for you to continue your adventure by heading towards the dunes of Erg Chebbi, possibly the largest dunes in the Sahara desert. The dunes of Erg Chebbi are a strikingly strange natural formation. On the top of the flattest area you could imagine, suddenly a long mountain of sand rises. This mountain is surrounded by flat and desolate nature on all sides, and you could end up wondering if it really is real. But so it is, even if its existence is so weird that it has given rise to legends and myths among the locals. Upon arrival at the camp you will witness the sunset from over the desert dunes and be astounded by the peace and calm as well as the changing colours of the landscape. If you’re up to it you can also ride a camel!
Accommodation at: Sahara Desert Camp (Standard).

itinerary.title: Merzouga – Erfoud – Ouarzazate
body: Transport (6hrs), Breakfast, Dinner, Driving distance: 390km

Leave the camp early morning after the sunrise, Take a camel ride back to the hotel for breakfast, and then contunie your journey with your private vehicle awaits for your onward journey. Travel today between Erfoud and Ouarzazate with private vehicle and English speaking driver. En-route, stop in the Dades Gorge, Todra Gorge’s more beautiful and older sister. These gorges are located just southwest of Tinerhir and some 110 km (65 miles) from Ouarzazate. In the latter winter, the Dades River flows and in mid-spring through early summer provides a life source to the valley`s unprecedented amount of greenery. In the valleys along the Dades Gorge, you’ll notice more argan (nut) trees more than the palmeries that surround the Todra Gorge. When you arrive at the top of the gorges, you will notice the temperatures will be cooler, the views amazing, and the people delightful. Northwest of Rissani and Northeast of Ouarzazate, just up the road from Tinerhir are the Todra Gorges. Experience the unbelievable glory of the massive canyon walls reaching some 300 meters (900 feet) high and continuing for some 100 meters (300 feet). A little north-east of the southern city of Quarzazate, lays the Dadès Valley-stretching out between the peaks of the High Atlas and the Jbel Sarhro Mountain range. Known as ‘The Valley of One Thousand Kasbahs’, it is the most prominent of the oasis valleys that dominate southern Morocco. Originating from melt water high up in the snowfields of the Haute Atlas, the river Dadès cuts a steep gorge, known as the Dadès Gorge, at Aït Oudinar and Aït Ali. From here, it flows across the broad Dadès Valley in a south-westerly direction towards Quarzazate. Before reaching Ouarzazate, you will make a stop in Skoura – one of Morocco’s beautiful oases. Skoura offers weary travellers a chance to rest their feet and enjoy the abundance of nature. At first glance from the road, it resembles a sort of thin, long, oasis but if you have a chance to explore within it, you will notice it is rather large and impressive. Continue to your lodging in the Ouarzazate area.
Accommodation at: Traditional Moroccan style Hotel (Standard).

itinerary.title: Ouarzazate – Ait Ben Hadou – Tichka Pass – Marrakech
body: Transport (4hrs), Breakfast, Dinner, Driving distance: 200km

Today leave Ouarzazate towards Marrakech, First stop will be in the village of Ait Ben Haddou. Located approximately 30 kilometers from Ouarzazate this fortified village (or ksar) is ideally positioned along a once frequented, ancient caravan route linking the Sahara and Marrakech. Ait Ben Haddou has been used in numerous Hollywood film productions for its distinctive architecture. In 1987 this famed location was deemed a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Next, travel to the village of Telouet, located approximately 1 hour north of Ait Ben Haddou. Telouet hosts one of the area’s most recognized structures, the palace of the ‘Lord of the Atlas.’ This palace was the residence of the once Vizier of Marrakech, back in the early 20th Century. An evocative relic of the time when the Glaoui clan ruled over the Atlas and Marrakech, the palace was the family’s Headquarters and was situated in a dramatic location, on a broad mountain valley, providing sweeping views of the peaks on all sides. Continue from here back onto the main road back to Marrakech, crossing on the dramatic Tizi n’Tichka passage through the High Atlas Mountains range on the way. Whilst passing take time to notice the many beautifully-terraced valleys and adobe villages perched precipitously on the hillsides, Arrive to Marrakech in the late aftrnoon.
Accommodation at: Traditional Moroccan style Hotel (Standard).

itinerary.title: Marrakech Guided Visit
body: Transport, Local English speaking guide, Breakfast

This morning around 9am your English speaking City tour guide will be meet you at your hotel/riad. And start your tour usually starts at the 12th century Koutoubia Mosque. This mosque’s beautiful minaret dominates the skyline of Marrakech and can be seen from almost every approach to the city thanks to a long-standing planning ordinance that forbids any other building in the old city to rise above the height of a palm tree. You will also visit the El-Bahia Palace, this 19th century palace is elaborate in its decoration and was built over a period of seven years for Ba Ahmed, the son of the Grand Vizier Si Moussa. There are row after row of apartments—that once housed Ahmed’s harem—a trapezoidal garden, a huge tiled courtyard, and many hidden treasures, both in the form of antique objects d’art and the palace’s convergence of Andalusian and Moorish architecture. One of most visited sites in Morocco is the Saadian Tombs which were only accessible via the mosque next door. However, in 1917 they were opened to the public and can now be accessed via a narrow passage that leads to an enclosed garden watched over by two mausoleums that include more than one hundred mosaic decorated tombs. The Koranic School Medersa Ben Youssef which is a Theological college founded by the Merenid Sultan Abu Hassan in the 14th century, and restored in 1564 by the Saadians who made it the largest theological college in the Maghreb and a rival to the important Medersa Bou Inania in Fés. Your tour lasts from 9:30am until 05:00pm
Accommodation at: Traditional Moroccan style Hotel (Standard).

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Atlas Mountain
body: Transport (3hrs), Breakfast, Lunch at Berber Family House or Picnic,Driving distance: 120km

After breakfast around 9am, your driver will be picked you up, And head south to the atlas Mountains, Youll meet your English speaking Mountain guide at the starting point of your option hike, Atlas Mountains Ouirgane (Wirgane) offers a great variety of optional activities. Choose between mountain biking, hiking, horseback and Mule riding, This morning from Marrakech, your guide and private vehicle will meet you at the hotel/riad at 09:00 in the morning to start the journey for 1h,30munte, and then Your hike will first go up to the Tirst Plateau and down to Ouirgane forest, full of junipers and pine trees. Following, you will continue to L’khmis Village, the village of Torourd , and then up through the Azaden Valley with very nice views of Takhrkhourt (large forest) in Toubkal National Park . Then, it is on to the Tasa Ouirgane with a small village. Here, we will have lunch in a local Berber family’s home and finally head back a different route to the Marigha and travel back to Marrakech. The hiking time will be flexible to you in between 1 – 5hrs hike.
Accommodation at: Traditional Moroccan style Hotel (Standard).

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Essaouira
body: Transport (3hrs), Breakfast, Driving distance: 180km

From Marrakech towards the coast Atlantic Essaouira. The approximate travel time is 3 hours. Enjoy a private tour of Essaouira, one of the most picturesque towns in the country. You will dive into its history and see how as an original Phoenician trading post, it prospered during the Roman era as citizens extracted the Tyrian purple colour from a local shellfish. Explore the fortifications that ring the city were built by the Portuguese and is inherent to the charm of Essaouira. You will have time to see the other attractions including the port, where a daily supply of fresh fish can be found, and the tremendous beach that stretches away to the south. The easy-going nature of the town, the medina, the dramatic fortifications and the beach, have created a bohemian atmosphere quite different from the rest of the country. At the end of the tour you will be transferred to your hotel in Essaouira.
Accommodation at: Traditional Moroccan style Hotel (Standard).

itinerary.title: Free Day in Essaouira
body: Transport, Breakfast

Today your driver will be at your disposal. Essaouira offers a great variety of optional activities. Choose between, relaxing in the beach horseback, fishing, surfing, wind surfing, kite surfing, camel rides, visits to Argan oil production, rural tourism.
Accommodation at: Traditional Moroccan style Hotel (Standard).

Your driver will provide a transfer between Essaouira and Casablanca or Marrakech. The approximate travel time in between Essaouira to Casablanca is 6 hrs, And 3hrs to Marrakech.
Today is the end of your trip, Here you’ll be say goodbye to our staff also our beautiful country Morocco, And going back home with good memories !

itinerary.title: Arrival in Casablanca – Rabat
body: Depending on your time of arrival, you might like to see some of the sights of Casablanca, in particular the Hassan II Mosque with the tallest minaret in the world. Casablanca (Spanish for “White House” and generally abbreviated by locals as “Casa”) has long stood in the western imagination as a hub of romance. Most travelers associate Casablanca with tales of the Marrakesh Express and, of course, the film, Casablanca. Of course, the reality of this fast-paced Moroccan city is quite different , you’ll visit the Hassan II Mosque it’s The largest mosque Morocco (and the 13th largest in the world) with the tallest minaret in the world. It was completed in 1993 and stands on the Northern Atlantic coast of Morocco, looking back over the Casablanca city line. Designed by Michel Pinseau and built by the Bourges, the minaret is 210 meters high and has a laser at the top which is directed towards Mecca. and then contunie your journey to Rabat , overnight at the Hotel/Riad .

itinerary.title: Rabat – Essaouira
body: Airport Transfer (5hrs 30minutes)
This morning after your breakfast you’ll visit of Rabat,

What is the capital of Morocco? Many people believe it’s Casablanca but in fact Rabat is the capital. In 1912 with the beginning of the French protectorate of Morocco the capital was moved from Fez to Rabat. In 1956 when independence was regained it was decided that the capital would stay put. Rabat isn’t on the tourist radar but there are many reasons to include it on your list. When it comes to seeing Morocco, Rabat is a bit of an unsung hero. The administrative capital is often left off the popular tourist circuit and folks tend to flock to Marrakech in the south and Fes, as well as Tangier and Chefchaouen in the central and northern parts of the country. Even Casablanca likely gets more traction than Rabat as it’s the location of the busiest international airport in Morocco as well as the largest mosque in North Africa, Hassan II , Kasbah Odayas ; Chellah Garden ; and then heading to Essaouira. The costal road offres beautiful scenery, an area famous for the Argan trees. Here you will see herds of goats climbing the Argan trees looking for better food than they can find on the ground. After several stops along the coast we get to Essaouira in the afternoon, Overnight accommodation at a riad in the Medina.

itinerary.title: Free Day to Explore Essaouirra ( Today you don’t need a guide its very samall and easy city to discover on your one ).
body: Transport, Breakfast

Breakfast at the hotel in Essaouira, then start your explorative journey of the city. You’ll visit the Skala Fortress; see Thuya wood carved by artisans; walk through the alleys of the medina and view hundreds of handicrafts. Today your driver can help you to have lunch in a Moroccan way, freshly bought fishes ‘cooked to order’. In the afternoon, you will have some free time to wander around , go to the beach and enjoy time to yourselves. Essaouira is also referred to as The “City of the Wind” and it attracts surfers from all over the world. Essaouira knew many civilizations – including the Portuguese occupation, which affects much of its architecture – however, it remains a small village with much history. Because of its size and its characteristic blue doors and washed walls, it is also regarded as Morocco’s “Jewel of the Atlantic”. There is an annual festival of “Gnawa music”, where many musical groups come from different parts of Africa and the world. Usually it starts in the second week of June. Overnight accommodation.

itinerary.title: Essaouirra – Marrakech
body: Transport (3hrs), Breakfast

After breakfast in your riad, you will have some free time before leaving for Marrakech. On our way – since this is the land of Argan culture – this is an opportunity to visit the women’s co-operative of Argan oil where they extract the oil that is famous for its culinary, cosmetic and medical properties. After several stops to take photographs, you will continue your travel to Marrakech and check in to your riad. After dinner you will have the option to enjoy walking within the famous square of Jemaa El fna, entertained with magicians, story tellers, musicians and snake charmers

itinerary.title: Marrakech Guided Tour
body: Private Guided Visit, Breakfast

This is your discovery day in the Red City, aided by your private guide who will meet with you in the morning at your riad to discuss the day’s possibilities. Leave the everyday behind as you dive into the souks, the markets that have provided Marrakschis with all their needs for over one thousand years. Vibrant colors, rich aromas, cat-calls and music, merchants in djellabas, street chefs in white hats, whatever your image of the exotic is you will find it in Marrakech. A visit to the Museum of Photography or the Majorelle Gardens are also highly recommended, visit the Souk, la Bahia Palace. Ali ben Youssef medersa (koranic school) & Musee de Marrakech to see the atrium), secret garden You can read more about our thoughts on the Red City in our Marrakesh travel guide Book that will give you a good understanding of what there is to see and do. The tour lasts from 9:30am until 5:30pm

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Atlas Mountains – Marrakech
body: Transport (2hrs), Breakfast, Lunch

This relaxed day trip will take you from the walls of the ‘Red City’ to the High Atlas hamlet of Ouirgane. En route you’ll make a stop at the busy little town of Asni which is a buzz of activity as local Berbers ply to sell their produce, particularly on Saturdays – market day. Once in Ouirgane your time is free to explore the village. Fed by the Oued Nfis from the Atlas, a perennial water source, the village is surprisingly verdant – a real oasis in the mountains. In recent years a dam was built creating a reservoir which adds to the visual appeal of the valley. Market day is Thursday in Ouirgane.

The most popular activity for visitors is walking – several circuits offer options for people of all abilities, from an hour’s stroll along village tracks, past typical Berber houses, farms and fields, to more challenging walks through the valley and along the river. Your guide will brief you on options when you arrive. Alternatively, enjoy the fresh mountain air and views from a cafe. Lunch is taken in a typical Berber village house, enjoying a home-cooked meal. After lunch you have time to discover more of the picturesque Ouirgane Valley, the timing its flexible from 1 to 4hrs, after the hike youll take a 1Hr journey back by car to Marrakech , overnight at the same riad .

tours.title: 8 Days Imperial Cities & Sahara Discovery Tour

seo.title: 8 Days Imperial Cities & Sahara Discovery Tour | Toubkal Peaks Travel Tours

summary: Embark on a journey through Morocco’s most iconic landscapes, from the bustling imperial cities to the endless golden dunes of the Sahara Desert. This 8-day adventure combines culture, history, and natural beauty, giving you a complete Moroccan experience.

Start in Casablanca, Morocco’s modern metropolis, and explore the imperial cities of Meknes and Fez, where ancient medinas, stunning palaces, and vibrant souks bring history to life. Travel through the Middle and High Atlas Mountains, stopping at cedar forests home to playful Barbary macaques, and marvel at the breathtaking gorges and valleys along the way.
highlights: Camel trek in the Sahara Desert & overnight in Bedouin-style camp
Azrou Cedar Forest & Barbary Macaques
Tizi N’Tichka Pass & High Atlas Mountains
Aït Ben Haddou (UNESCO Site)
Atlas Film Studios (Gladiator, Game of Thrones)

itinerary.title: Arrival in Casablanca
body: Distance / Duration: Airport transfer only
Welcome to Morocco! Upon arrival at Casablanca Mohammed V International Airport, you’ll be greeted by your driver and transferred to your hotel.

Depending on your arrival time, you can visit the magnificent Hassan II Mosque, one of the world’s largest mosques, set dramatically on the Atlantic coast. Take a stroll along the Corniche or enjoy dinner in one of the city’s lively restaurants.

itinerary.title: Casablanca → Meknes → Moulay Idriss → Volubilis → Fez
body: After breakfast, depart for the Imperial City of Meknes, founded by Sultan Moulay Ismail. Visit Bab Mansour, El Hedim Square, and the Royal Stables, then continue to Moulay Idriss Zerhoun, Morocco’s holiest town.

Next, explore the nearby Roman ruins of Volubilis, a UNESCO World Heritage site renowned for its well-preserved mosaics and arches. Arrive in Fez by evening and settle into your charming riad within the ancient medina.
Meals: Breakfast included

itinerary.title: Full-Day Guided Tour of Fez
body: Walking tour inside the medina

Spend a full day discovering Fez el-Bali, the spiritual and cultural heart of Morocco. With your local guide, wander the labyrinth of narrow alleys filled with tanneries, spice markets, mosques, and artisan workshops.
Highlights include:
- Bou Inania Madrasa – one of the finest Islamic schools in Morocco
- Karaouiyine Mosque & University – the oldest continuously operating university in the world
- Nejjarine Fountain and the Medersa el-Attarine
- The Royal Palace and Jewish Quarter (Mellah)
Evening at leisure to relax or enjoy dinner at a local restaurant with traditional music.
Meals: Breakfast included

itinerary.title: Fez → Ifrane → Azrou Cedar Forest → Midelt → Ziz Valley → Merzouga (Camel Trek & Desert Camp)
itinerary.accommodation: Desert camp in Merzouga (standard or luxury)
body: Today’s drive takes you across the Middle Atlas Mountains and into the Sahara Desert. Stop in Ifrane, known as the Switzerland of Morocco, then continue through the cedar forest of Azrou, home to Barbary macaques.
Lunch in Midelt before descending into the Ziz Valley, famous for its lush palm groves and traditional kasbahs.

Arrive at Merzouga in the late afternoon, where your camel caravan awaits. Ride across the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi at sunset to reach your desert camp. Enjoy mint tea, Berber music, and dinner under a canopy of stars.
Meals: Breakfast & Dinner included

itinerary.title: Merzouga → Tinjdad → Todra Gorge → Dades Valley → Ouarzazate
body: Wake early to witness the sunrise over the dunes, then ride camels (or 4×4 transfer) back to Merzouga village. After breakfast, travel through Erfoud and Tinjdad toward the breathtaking Todra Gorge, where 300-metre cliffs rise dramatically above the valley floor.
Enjoy a short walk through the gorge before continuing via Boumalne Dades and along the scenic Road of a Thousand Kasbahs to reach Ouarzazate, Morocco’s “Gateway to the Desert.”
Meals: Breakfast & Dinner included

itinerary.title: Ouarzazate → Aït Ben Haddou → High Atlas Mountains → Marrakech
body: After breakfast, visit the Kasbah of Taourirt and the Atlas Film Studios, where many Hollywood films such as Gladiator and The Mummy were shot. Continue to Aït Ben Haddou, a UNESCO-listed ksar made of earthen clay and straw — one of Morocco’s most iconic landmarks.
After lunch, cross the spectacular High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n’Tichka Pass (2,260 m), enjoying panoramic views and Berber villages en route. Arrive in Marrakech by late afternoon.
Meals: Breakfast included

itinerary.title: Marrakech Guided City Tour
body: Walking tour inside the Medina
Discover the magic of Marrakech, known as the “Red City.” Your local guide will take you through the highlights:
- Koutoubia Mosque and its 12th-century minaret
- Bahia Palace and Saadian Tombs
- The Majorelle Gardens (optional visit)
- The bustling souks and the vibrant Jemaa el-Fna Square, alive with storytellers, musicians, and food stalls.
Evening free to relax at your riad or enjoy a rooftop dinner overlooking the medina.
Meals: Breakfast included
