tours.title: 8 Days Morocco Imperial Cities, Mountains & Desert Tour

seo.title: 8 Days Morocco Imperial Cities, Mountains & Desert Tour | Toubkal Peaks Travel Tours

itinerary.title: Arrival in Casablanca – Hassan II Mosque & Seaside Promenade
body: Your Moroccan adventure begins as you land at Casablanca Mohammed V International Airport, where you will be greeted and transferred to the city. Depending on your arrival time, you’ll enjoy a first introduction to Morocco’s largest city, the country’s economic and cultural hub.

The highlight today is a visit to the Hassan II Mosque, one of the largest mosques in the world and an icon of Moroccan architecture. Built partly over the Atlantic Ocean, its 210-meter minaret towers over the city, while the interiors dazzle with hand-carved cedar, marble, and traditional zellij tilework.
Later, take a leisurely walk along the Corniche seaside promenade, where cafés and ocean views set the tone for your journey. The evening is free to relax and prepare for the adventure ahead.
Overnight in Casablanca.
Distance: Airport → City center: 30 km / ~45 minutes

itinerary.title: Casablanca – Meknes – Volubilis – Fez
body: After breakfast, depart for Meknes, once the capital of Morocco under Sultan Moulay Ismail. The drive takes you through rolling countryside before reaching this imperial city known as the “Versailles of Morocco.” Visit Bab Mansour, one of the most impressive city gates in North Africa, and explore El Hedim Square, where locals gather around food stalls and storytellers. You will also step inside the Royal Granaries & Stables, once designed to feed the entire city and house the Sultan’s 12,000 horses.

A short drive leads you to Volubilis, the ancient Roman city and UNESCO World Heritage Site. Stroll through the remarkably preserved ruins, admiring the mosaics, triumphal arch, and remnants of Roman villas while learning about Morocco’s importance in the Roman Empire.
Continue through the fertile Saiss plains, dotted with olive groves and vineyards, before arriving in Fez, Morocco’s cultural and spiritual capital.
Overnight in Fez.
Distance: Casablanca → Meknes 240 km (~3 hrs). Meknes → Volubilis 30 km (~45 mins). Volubilis → Fez 90 km (~1.5 hrs). Total: ~360 km / ~5–6 hrs driving

itinerary.title: Fez – Full-Day Guided Exploration of the Medina
body: Today is dedicated to discovering the treasures of Fez el-Bali, the old city of Fez and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This labyrinthine Medina is the world’s largest car-free urban area, filled with bustling souks, workshops, and hidden gems.

Begin at the ornate Bab Boujloud (Blue Gate) before entering the winding alleys where donkeys remain the main mode of transport. Visit the Bou Inania Madrasa, a 14th-century Quranic school showcasing beautiful cedar and stucco work. From there, continue to the colorful Chouara Tanneries, where leather is dyed in large stone vats using centuries-old techniques.

Your exploration also takes you to the University of Al-Qarawiyyin, founded in 859 and recognized as the oldest university in the world still in operation. Wander through artisan quarters where brassworkers, weavers, and potters continue ancient crafts.

In the afternoon, visit Fez el-Jdid, the Royal Palace gates, and the historic Mellah (Jewish Quarter). End the day with panoramic views over the Medina from Borj Nord fortress before returning to your riad.
Overnight in Fez.
Minimal driving – mostly walking inside the Medina

itinerary.title: Fez – Cooking Class & Free Afternoon
body: This morning offers a hands-on cultural experience as you join a traditional Moroccan cooking class. Begin with a visit to a lively local market, where your chef will introduce you to Moroccan spices, fresh herbs, and seasonal ingredients. Back in the kitchen, learn how to prepare a variety of classic dishes such as aromatic tagines, fluffy couscous, or the sweet-and-savory pastilla.

After enjoying your home-cooked lunch, the afternoon is free for personal discovery. You may choose to stroll through artisan workshops, visit the pottery quarter of Fez, or simply relax in a tranquil riad. For those seeking rejuvenation, a traditional hammam and spa experience can also be arranged.
Overnight in Fez.
Activities within the city – no major transfers required

itinerary.title: Fez – Agafay Desert (via Marrakech)
body: Today is a day of contrasts as you leave Fez and journey south. The drive passes through ever-changing scenery, from fertile valleys to olive groves and the arid landscapes of central Morocco. Arrive in vibrant Marrakech by afternoon before continuing into the nearby Agafay Desert, a rocky plateau at the edge of the Atlas Mountains.

Upon arrival, you’ll trade wheels for a camel or quad bike and ride into the desert terrain as the sun begins to set over the horizon. Unlike the sand dunes of the Sahara, Agafay offers a dramatic lunar-like setting, especially stunning against the snow-capped Atlas peaks in the distance.
Tonight, gather around the fire for music, storytelling, and a magical evening under the stars. A traditional Moroccan dinner will be served at your luxury desert camp.
Overnight in Agafay Desert Camp.
Distance: Fez → Marrakech 530 km (~6.5–7 hrs). Marrakech → Agafay Desert 35 km (~45 mins). Total: ~565 km / ~7.5 hrs

itinerary.title: Agafay Desert – High Atlas Mountains – Marrakech
body: After breakfast, depart the Agafay Desert and head into the High Atlas Mountains. Winding roads take you through valleys, orchards, and Berber villages, where traditional life has changed little over centuries.

You will enjoy a guided hike (1–2 hours) through terraced fields, walnut groves, and mountain paths with sweeping views. Midday, share a home-cooked lunch with a local Berber family, a memorable experience that allows you to connect with Morocco’s mountain culture.
In the afternoon, return to Marrakech, where the rest of the day is at leisure. You may choose to relax in your riad, wander the souks, or sip tea in a rooftop café overlooking the lively streets.
Overnight in Marrakech.
Distance: Agafay → High Atlas ~65 km (~1.5 hrs). High Atlas → Marrakech ~60 km (~1.5 hrs). Total: ~125 km / ~3 hrs

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Guided City Tour
body: Today you will discover the highlights of Marrakech, Morocco’s “Red City.” Begin at the Koutoubia Mosque, an architectural masterpiece from the 12th century with its iconic minaret visible across the city. Continue to the Bahia Palace, a 19th-century residence filled with gardens, mosaics, and ornate courtyards. Nearby, the Saadian Tombs, rediscovered in 1917, reveal the grandeur of Morocco’s Saadian dynasty.

In the afternoon, explore the colorful Majorelle Garden, designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Its cobalt-blue walls and exotic plants make it one of Marrakech’s most photographed sites.

Your tour concludes in the vibrant souks and the legendary Jemaa el-Fna square, a UNESCO-listed cultural space where snake charmers, musicians, acrobats, and food stalls create an unforgettable atmosphere.
Overnight in Marrakech.
Minimal transfers inside the city – mostly walking & short drives

itinerary.title: Departure from Marrakech (or Casablanca)
body: Depending on your flight schedule, you will be transferred to either Marrakech Airport or Casablanca Airport. Your driver will ensure you arrive on time for your departure, carrying with you unforgettable memories of Morocco’s imperial cities, desert landscapes, and mountain hospitality.
End of services.
Marrakech → Airport: 10 km / 20–30 mins. Marrakech → Casablanca Airport: 230 km / ~3 hrs

seo.title: 8 Days The Great South of Morocco Tour | Toubkal Peaks Travel Tours

summary: Embark on a fascinating 8-day journey through the Great South of Morocco, exploring dramatic landscapes, historic kasbahs, Berber villages, and the golden dunes of the Sahara Desert.
This well-paced tour combines culture, adventure, and comfort, starting and ending in Marrakech — the perfect introduction to Morocco’s natural and cultural treasures.

itinerary.title: Welcome Arrival in Marrakech
body: - Distance / Driving: N/A
- Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport, where your friendly driver will greet you and escort you to your riad. Take the afternoon to relax and absorb the vibrant atmosphere of the Red City.

- If time allows, wander through Jemaa El Fna Square, a lively hub of storytellers, musicians, and street food vendors. Explore the nearby souks filled with spices, textiles, and handicrafts, or enjoy a refreshing Moroccan mint tea at a terrace café.

itinerary.title: Marrakech → Ouarzazate → Kelaat M’Gouna → Dades Valley
body: Distance: ~360 km | Driving Time: 7–8 hours

- Begin your journey across the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n’Tichka Pass (2260 m), where panoramic views of jagged peaks and traditional Berber villages await. Stop for photos at scenic viewpoints.
- Continue to Ouarzazate, known as the “Gateway to the Sahara,” and home to historic kasbahs and film studios. Pause for lunch and enjoy the dramatic desert landscapes.

- Drive through the Rose Valley (Kelaat M’Gouna), famous for its fragrant roses and seasonal rose festivals. End the day in the Dades Valley, celebrated for its striking red cliffs and “Monkey Fingers” rock formations.
Meals: Breakfast & Dinner

itinerary.title: Dades Valley → Todra Gorge → Tinjdad → Erfoud → Merzouga
body: - Depart for Todra Gorge, where towering cliffs rise 300 meters high. Take a leisurely walk along the river or simply marvel at the sheer canyon walls.
- Continue to Tinjdad for lunch, a small town offering a glimpse of rural life in the desert region.
- Drive through Erfoud, a town famous for its ancient fossils and dates. You can visit a local fossil workshop if interested.
- Arrive in Merzouga, the gateway to the Erg Chebbi dunes, where golden sands stretch as far as the eye can see. Witness your first Saharan sunset before heading to your accommodation.
Meals: Breakfast & Dinner

itinerary.title: Exploring Merzouga & Desert Experience
body: - Begin with a visit to Hassi Labied Garden Oasis, a serene spot of palm groves and desert flora.
- Depending on the season, explore Merzouga Lake, a seasonal haven for migratory birds such as flamingos.
- Visit Khamlia Village, home of the Gnawa musicians, and enjoy traditional music and dance performances.
- Savor a Berber pizza lunch in a local home.

- In the afternoon, relax at your accommodation or pool before embarking on a camel trek into the towering Erg Chebbi dunes. Experience the magic of the desert as the sun sets over endless sand dunes.
- Arrive at your desert camp for a traditional dinner, evening drumming, and a night under a blanket of stars.
Meals: Breakfast & Dinner

itinerary.title: Merzouga → Rissani → Alnif → Nkoub → Agdz → Aït Ben Haddou
body: - Wake early to witness a breathtaking Sahara sunrise over the dunes. Return via camel to your meeting point and enjoy breakfast.
- Drive north through Rissani, the ancient trading town, and explore its lively markets if time permits. Continue through Alnif and Nkoub, villages that showcase rural Berber life.
- Travel along the scenic Draa Valley, known for its lush palm groves and ancient kasbahs.
- Arrive at Aït Ben Haddou, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of Morocco’s most famous kasbahs. Its earthen architecture has featured in numerous films including “Gladiator” and “Game of Thrones.”
Meals: Breakfast & Dinner

itinerary.title: Aït Ben Haddou → Marrakech
body: - Enjoy a guided visit of Aït Ben Haddou, exploring narrow alleys, ancient towers, and traditional Berber houses. Capture memorable photos of the fortified village perched against the desert backdrop.
- Drive back over the High Atlas Mountains via Tizi n’Tichka Pass. Stop for photos at viewpoints, reflecting on the contrast between rugged mountains and the desert plains.
Meals: Breakfast

itinerary.title: Guided Tour of Marrakech
body: - Spend the day exploring Marrakech’s highlights:
- Majorelle Gardens: A peaceful oasis with vibrant blue architecture and exotic plants.
- Koutoubia Mosque: Admire the iconic minaret from outside (non-Muslim visitors cannot enter).
- Bahia Palace: Marvel at intricate mosaics, courtyards, and gardens.
- Medina & Souks: Wander through bustling markets filled with spices, textiles, pottery, and handicrafts.
- Optional: Enjoy a traditional Moroccan lunch in the medina.
Meals: Breakfast

itinerary.title: Departure
body: - Transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for your return flight or onward journey.
- Reflect on a journey filled with deserts, mountains, kasbahs, and vibrant Moroccan culture.
Meals: Breakfast

Depending on your arrival time, enjoy a short stroll around the city or relax at your accommodation. This is a great time to soak in the atmosphere of Morocco’s vibrant streets, enjoy mint tea, and prepare for the adventure ahead.

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Guided City Tour
body: - Highlights: Koutoubia Mosque, Bahia Palace, Saadian Tombs
- Markets & Souks: Jemaa el-Fna square – street performers, snake charmers, local food stalls
- Overnight: Marrakech

Description: Explore Marrakech with a professional guide, learning about Moroccan history, architecture, and culture. Wander through the medina’s labyrinthine streets and bustling souks, where spices, ceramics, carpets, and artisan crafts abound. End the day in Jemaa el-Fna, experiencing the city’s lively energy.

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Imlil (High Atlas Mountains) – Hike & Lunch
body: - Distance: ~65 km / 1.5–2 hrs drive
- Activity: Moderate hike through Berber villages, valleys, and terraced fields
- Lunch: Traditional Moroccan meal in Imlil
- Overnight: Imlil

Description: Journey into the High Atlas Mountains to the village of Imlil. Embark on a scenic hike through picturesque valleys and small Berber villages, enjoying panoramic views and local hospitality. Stop for a traditional Moroccan lunch with stunning mountain vistas. Evening at leisure in a cozy riad.

itinerary.title: Imlil – Ait Ben Haddou – Ouarzazate – Kelaa Mgouna – Dades Valley
body: - Distance: ~360 km / 7–8 hrs drive with stops
- Highlights:
- Tizi n’Tichka Pass (2,260 m) – panoramic Atlas views
- Ait Ben Haddou – UNESCO-listed kasbah and film location
- Ouarzazate – “Hollywood of Morocco”

Description: Drive through the High Atlas, stopping at breathtaking viewpoints along the Tizi n’Tichka Pass. Explore the iconic Ait Ben Haddou, an ancient fortified village featured in many films. Continue to Ouarzazate and Kelaa Mgouna, known for its rose fields, before arriving in the picturesque Dades Valley, famous for its striking cliffs and rock formations.

itinerary.title: Dades Valley – Todra Gorge – Tinejdad – Arfoud – Merzouga (Camel Trek & Desert Camp)
body: - Distance: ~300 km / 6–7 hrs drive
- Highlights: Todra Gorge – towering canyon cliffs
- Activity: Camel trek into Erg Chebbi dunes at sunset
- Overnight: Desert camp under the stars

Description: Journey from the Dades Valley through Todra Gorge, marveling at its towering cliffs. Pass through Tinejdad and Arfoud, small desert towns en route to Merzouga. Experience a traditional camel trek into the Sahara dunes, arriving at your desert camp in time for sunset. Enjoy a dinner under the stars with music and storytelling for an authentic desert experience.

itinerary.title: Merzouga – Ziz Valley – Azrou – Ifrane – Fez
body: - Distance: ~470 km / 8–9 hrs drive
- Highlights: Ziz Valley – lush palm groves and historic kasbahs

- Overnight: Fez

Description: Depart the Sahara and travel through the Ziz Valley with its oasis-like palm groves. Stop in Azrou to see the cedar forests and the famous Barbary monkeys. Continue via Ifrane, nicknamed “Little Switzerland” for its European-style architecture. Arrive in Fez in the evening.

itinerary.title: Fez – Guided City Visit
body: - Highlights: Fez el-Bali Medina, Bou Inania Madrasa, Chouara Tanneries, University of Al-Qarawiyyin, Fez el-Jdid, Royal Palace gates, Mellah (Jewish Quarter)
- Overnight: Fez

Description: Explore Fez’s medieval medina with a local guide. Discover artisans at work in leather, metal, and pottery workshops. Visit historic religious and educational landmarks, and gain insight into Morocco’s rich culture and traditions. The day concludes with panoramic views of the medina from Borj Nord.

tours.title: Tour From Casablanca Morocco City To City ( 13Days/12Nights )

seo.title: Tour From Casablanca Morocco City To City ( 13Days/12Nights ) | Toubkal Peaks Travel Tours

itinerary.title: Arrive in Casablanca – Rabat
body: Airport Transfer (2hrs), Dinner

Welcome to Morocco! It’s possible to start your trip in either Casablanca/Rabat . Upon arrival, you will be collected and taken to your hotel to unwind and relax. If you have time to spare, on your way to Rabat you can stop and visit the Hasan II mosque, and then continue your journey to Rabat , overnight in Rabat.

itinerary.title: Rabat – Volubilis – Fez
body: Transport (4hrs), Breakfast

Depart for Fes. The road to Fes takes us along a beautiful stretch of farmlands where olives, grain, vegetables and grapes are grown. Before arriving to Fes you will visit Meknes and Volubilis. Volubilis is the sight of the famous Roman ruins left from the Roman Empire’s most southern outpost. Meknes is the site of the first Arab dynasty created by Moulay Ismail and has the Medersa Bou Inania and the Bab Mansour, the Gateway to Moulay Ismail Palace. This leads us into the Henri es-Souani, the horses stable and granaries. Upstairs is a rooftop garden and cafe with a great view of the city. Arrive into Fes, check into the hotel.

itinerary.title: Fez Guided Visit
body: Transport , Breakfast

After breakfast, you will begin your visit of Fes “the oldest living Medina in the world” with a local official tour guide. You will tour the Medina with its “souks” (markets), stopping at the gateway of the Royal Palace, the 9th century Karouine mosque and University. You will visit also the tomb of the city founder “Moulay Idriss II”. Lunch will be at one of the traditional restaurants in the old Medina. After lunch you will continue your tour to visit the Najarine Fountain, the old Harem Garden and the Batha Museum. On the way back to the hotel, you will stop to enjoy a panoramic view of the city.

itinerary.title: Fez – Ziz Valley – Merzouga
body: Transport (7hrs) , Breakfast , Dinner

After breakfast we will start our day to Merzouga crossing the Atlas Mountains, passing through Ifrane to arrive to the cedar forests of Azrou where the wild monkeys are located. It will be good opportunity to take photos of wilderness in Morocco. Lunch in a small Berber village of Zaida. We continue the way through the Atlas Mountains enjoying the landscapes of Medilt to arrive to the small town of Rich, Erfoud in which we’ll feel the beginning of the Saharan oasis of Tafilalet then we continue to Merzouga, Overnight in a hotel near the dunes.

itinerary.title: Merzouga – Gnaoua Music – Camel Ride , Desert Camp
body: Transport (1hr), Breakfast , Dinner

After breakfast in the hotel you’ll start your explorative desert journey of the area, visiting the village of Khamlia, originally slaves from Sudan to experience their music and lifestyle. Not far away there’s the lake of Merzouga, with its bird populations, including flamingos. You may also like to visit the nomad wire house where many Berber handicrafts are priced lower than in the big cities. On the afternoon you will ride camel, guided by an experienced Camel man, to explore inside the mysterious sand-sea of the Erg-Chebbi. Here you’ll spend your first night under the stars, or if you prefer, in a traditional Berber nomad tent. Dinner will be served in the tent where you will spend the night. Dinner Bed and Breakfast.

itinerary.title: Desert Camp – Todra Gorge – Ouarzazate or Ait Ben Haddou
body: Transport (6hrs), Breakfast , Dinner

After breakfast in the hotel we’ll drive through the Dades Valley towards Kalaa M’gouna and Ouarzazat. The route through Dades Valley is the way of the thousand kasbahs – providing numerous opportunities to take some of your best photographic shots of the trip. We’ll stop at Kalaa Mgouna, “the rose city”, to purchase the rosewater, which will make your linen smell good a long time after your trip is over. Continue to Skoura and the dirds valley; visit the Kasbah Ameridil, a well-preserved kasbah in this area. After lunch, you will have some time for hiking within the valley and then continue to Ouarzazate – “the Hollywood of Africa”- whose geography and beautiful landscapes have attracted many world class movie producers, Overnight accommodation will be in riad.

itinerary.title: Ouarzazate – Taznakhte – Taroudant
body: Transport (4hrs), Breakfast

After breakfast in your riad, we’ll head to Taroudant via Taznakht, visiting Ait Ben Haddou Kasbah, the largest Kasbah in Morocco. Built during the beginning of the XXth Century by T-hami El Glaoui -one of the last Berber chieftains -Ben Haddou Kasbah used to be one of his stops during his long travel from the sub-Saharan countries to Marrakech, and is now a UNESCO world heritage site. On to Taliouine, the capital of saffron in Morocco, you have the option to visit the Safran co-operative. If your visit coincides with the saffron harvest, you will have the opportunity to meet the Berber people with their families harvesting the saffron in their fields. We should arrive at Taroudant in the afternoon, here you will see the ramparts and walk within the small alleys in the Medina. Taroudant is always referred to as “The little Marrakech” because it was the built by the Saadian dynasty who used it as their capital before they moved to Marrakech in the 16th century.

itinerary.title: Taroudant – Agadir – Essaouira
body: Transport (4h30m), Breakfast

Breakfast in the riad, and then head for Essaouira, travelling via Agadir. Our first stop will be at Agadir, a resort city which was a very big tourist destination for many years. After lunch and a small walk along the Promenade, you will continue to Essaouira. The coastal road offers beautiful scenery, an area famous for the Argan trees. Here you will see herds of goats climbing the Argan trees looking for better food than they can find on the ground. After several stops along the coast we get to Essaouira in the afternoon. Overnight accommodation at a riad in the Medina.

itinerary.title: Free day in Essaouira
body: Breakfast at the hotel in Essaouira, then start our explorative journey of the city. You’ll visit the Skala Fortress; see Thuya wood carved by artisans; walk through the alleys of the medina and view hundreds of handicrafts. Today you will have lunch in a Moroccan way, freshly bought fishes ‘cooked to order’. In the afternoon, you will have some free time to wander around , go to the beach and enjoy time to yourselves. Essaouira is also referred to as The “City of the Wind” and it attracts surfers from all over the world. Essaouira knew many civilisations – including the Portuguese occupation, which affects much of its architecture – however, it remains a small village with much history. Because of its size and its characteristic blue doors and washed walls, it is also regarded as Morocco’s “Jewel of the Atlantic”. There is an annual festival of “Gnawa music”, where many musical groups come from different parts of Africa and the world. Usually it starts in the second week of June.

itinerary.title: Essaouira – Marrakech
body: Transport (2h30m), Breakfast

After breakfast in your riad, you will have some free time before leaving for Marrakech. On our way – since this is the land of Argan culture – this is an opportunity to visit the women’s co-operative of Argan oil where they extract the oil that is famous for its culinary, cosmetic and medical properties. After several stops to take photographs, you will continue your travel to Marrakech and check in to your riad. After dinner you will have the option to enjoy walking within the famous square of Jemaa El fna, entertained with magicians, story tellers, musicians and snake charmers.

itinerary.title: Marrakech Guided Tour
body: Transport , Breakfast

A full-day tour of Marrakech, visit the Menara, a surrounded pool by flowerbeds that function as an irrigation system for the surrounded fields. The sightseeing tour will cover several impressive sights: The Koutoubia mosque, Majorelle Gardens, Bahia Palace and Dar Si Said Palace museum of jewellery. Optional lunch will be in the medina followed by a walk through the colorful souks of Marrakech. Enjoy a sunset drink overlooking the exciting Jamaa El Fna Square from a terrace of a cafe, dinner and night at hotel.

itinerary.title: High Atlas Mountains
body: Transport (3hrs around the trip), Breakfast

One day trip from Marrakech to Ouirgane Valley start in the morning departure from Marrakech to Ouirgane Valley, the easiest, closest and thus one of the best day trips from Marrakech. On our Ouirgane day trip you’ll travel on a private tour with your own vehicle, driver and guide. To achieve a truly authentic Ouirgane Valley experience we aim to avoid the typical tourist traps and focus on real Berber village life including lunch with a Berber family, the food is fresh and organic, also you’ll have optionally for having a hike in the heart of the National park and visiting a several Berber villages in the valley, exploring local trails on foot far away from the fleets of tour buses…you’ll be going back to Marrakech in evening.

itinerary.title: Marrakech → Ait Ben Haddou → Ouarzazate → Draa Valley → Zagora (Desert Camp)
body: Distance: ~360 km | Driving time: 7–8 hours (with sightseeing stops)

- After breakfast, departure from Marrakech in a private vehicle. The adventure begins by crossing the High Atlas Mountains via the winding Tizi n’Tichka Pass (2,260 m) . Along the way, you’ll pass terraced fields, small Berber villages clinging to the mountainsides, and dramatic valleys perfect for photos.

- Stop at Ait Ben Haddou , the most famous ksar (fortified village) in Morocco, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. This ancient mud-brick citadel has featured in films such as Gladiator, Lawrence of Arabia, and Game of Thrones. Explore its narrow lanes and take in panoramic views from the top.

- Continue to Ouarzazate, known as the “Hollywood of Africa” thanks to its film studios and desert scenery. Optional stop at the Taourirt Kasbah, a historic fortress once belonging to the Glaoui family.

- From here, the road leads into the Draa Valley, Morocco’s longest oasis , stretching nearly 200 km with lush palm groves, fortified villages (ksour), and ancient kasbahs. The valley is the gateway to the Sahara and offers endless photo opportunities.
- Arrive in Zagora by late afternoon. Meet your camel caravan for a sunset camel trek across the desert landscape.
- Evening arrival at your desert camp, where you’ll enjoy a traditional dinner under the stars and live Berber drumming around the campfire.

itinerary.title: Zagora → Agdz → Anti-Atlas → Ouarzazate → Marrakech
body: - Wake early to witness the breathtaking sunrise over the desert dunes , a magical moment as the first light paints the Sahara in golden tones.
- After breakfast, return by camel or 4×4 to Zagora town.

- Drive back along the Draa Valley, with more time to enjoy the palm groves, traditional ksour, and small mud-brick villages. Stop in Agdz, a charming town with views of the Jebel Kissane Mountains and hundreds of kasbahs scattered among the palms.
- Cross the Anti-Atlas Mountains, a region of rugged landscapes and dramatic gorges.
- Arrive again in Ouarzazate for a lunch break or optional visit to a kasbah or film studio.
- Continue across the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n’Tichka Pass, descending gradually back toward Marrakech. Expect panoramic views, winding roads, and small Berber villages along the way.
- Evening arrival in Marrakech (around 19:00–20:00), drop-off at your hotel/riad.

Your adventure begins with a scenic drive over the Tizi n’Tichka Pass (2,260 m) , passing terraced slopes, traditional Berber villages, and panoramic viewpoints. Explore the iconic Ait Ben Haddou Kasbah , a UNESCO World Heritage Site and famous filming location, then continue through Ouarzazate, Morocco’s “Hollywood of Africa” .

itinerary.title: Marrakech → High Atlas Mountains → Ait Ben Haddou → Ouarzazate → Dades Valley
body: - Depart Marrakech early in the morning . Cross the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n’Tichka Pass (2,260 m) . Along the way, enjoy panoramic views, traditional Berber villages, and terraced slopes.

- Stop at Ait Ben Haddou Kasbah , a UNESCO World Heritage Site and famous filming location for Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Walk through narrow streets, admire the ancient mud-brick towers, and take photos from the hilltop viewpoint.
- Continue to Ouarzazate, the “Hollywood of Africa” . Optional short visit to Taourirt Kasbah or one of the local film studios to experience Morocco’s cinematic history.
- Drive through Skoura Oasis , known for its lush palm groves and historic kasbahs. Take photos of the oasis and stop at scenic viewpoints along the way.
- Arrive in the Dades Valley, famous for its dramatic red cliffs, winding roads, and ancient kasbahs perched on the rocks.
- Overnight: Guesthouse or riad in Dades Valley, with dinner included.

itinerary.title: Dades Valley → Todra Gorge → Merzouga Desert
body: - Depart early from Dades Valley and continue along the “Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs” . Stop at panoramic viewpoints to admire the kasbahs, red cliffs, and oasis villages along the road.

- Visit Todra Gorge , a spectacular canyon with sheer cliffs reaching over 300 meters high. Take a short walk at the base, enjoy the dramatic scenery, and capture photos of the gorge’s unique geology.
- Continue east towards Merzouga, passing small desert towns and watching the landscape transition from mountains and palm oases to the golden Sahara sands .
- Arrive in Merzouga, the gateway to the Erg Chebbi dunes. Meet your camels and ride into the dunes to reach your desert camp.
- Enjoy a sunset over the Sahara, one of Morocco’s most magical experiences.
- Dinner under the stars with traditional Berber music and overnight in the desert camp .

itinerary.title: Merzouga → Rissani → Erfoud → Ziz Valley → Midelt → Ifrane → Fez

summary: Embark on an unforgettable adventure through Morocco’s southeast on this 3-day desert journey. From the bustling streets of Marrakech to the golden sands of the Sahara, this trip offers a perfect combination of scenic landscapes, cultural experiences, and desert adventure.

Travel across the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n’Tichka Pass , passing traditional Berber villages, terraced valleys, and panoramic viewpoints. Explore the legendary Ait Ben Haddou Kasbah , a UNESCO World Heritage site, and witness the historic kasbahs scattered throughout the Skoura Oasis and Dades Valley .

itinerary.title: Marrakech → High Atlas Mountains → Ait Ben Haddou → Ouarzazate → Dades Valley

- Stop at the iconic Ait Ben Haddou Kasbah , a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore the narrow lanes, mud-brick towers, and take photos from the hilltop viewpoint. Famous filming location for movies like Gladiator and Game of Thrones.
- Continue to Ouarzazate, Morocco’s film capital . Optional visit to the Taourirt Kasbah, an impressive fortress that once belonged to the Glaoui family, and/or a short stop at local film studios.

- Drive through Skoura Oasis , a lush palm grove dotted with kasbahs. Capture the beauty of the valley, visit a traditional kasbah if time allows, and enjoy photo stops of the Dades Valley’s striking red rock landscapes.

itinerary.title: Dades Valley / Skoura → Todra Gorge → Merzouga Desert

tours.title: 4 Days Sahara Desert Trip From Fes to Marrakech

seo.title: 4 Days Sahara Desert Trip From Fes to Marrakech | Toubkal Peaks Travel Tours

summary: This unforgettable 4-day desert adventure takes you from the spiritual city of Fes to the lively streets of Marrakech, crossing Morocco’s most enchanting regions. Travel through Ifrane’s alpine charm, meet monkeys in the cedar forests of Azrou , and descend into the golden Sahara dunes of Merzouga . Ride a camel into the desert, enjoy Berber music under the stars, and explore the dramatic Todra Gorge and lush valleys of roses . End your journey in Aït Benhaddou’s ancient kasbahs before winding through the High Atlas Mountains to arrive in Marrakech. A perfect balance of adventure, culture, and breathtaking scenery.

itinerary.title: Fes – Ifrane – Azrou – Midelt – Merzouga
body: Your adventure begins with a scenic drive south from Fes into the Middle Atlas Mountains. The first stop is in Ifrane, often called the “Switzerland of Morocco” for its alpine-style houses and clean mountain air. Continuing on, we pass through Azrou, famous for its cedar forests where you’ll have the chance to see Barbary macaque monkeys in their natural habitat.

We then cross the Tizi n’Talghamt Pass and continue to Midelt, a small town known for its apple orchards and breathtaking mountain views. From here, the landscape transforms dramatically as we follow the Ziz Gorges, carved into volcanic rock, and descend towards the Sahara. The scenery shifts from lush mountains to dry plateaus, with the first golden hints of desert dunes appearing on the horizon.
After a break for lunch near Errachidia, we continue through the palm-filled Ziz Valley , dotted with traditional mud-brick villages, before arriving in Erfoud, the gateway to the Sahara Desert.
Overnight in a traditional Moroccan-style hotel in Merzouga, where you’ll enjoy dinner and prepare for the desert adventure ahead.

itinerary.title: Merzouga Desert Exploration – Khamlia Village – Camel Ride – Sahara Camp
body: Distance: ~40 km local exploration
Travel Time: 3–4 hrs of easy driving (with visits)
Camel Ride: ~1 hr each way (sunset & sunrise)
Meals: Breakfast & Dinner included
Day Highlights
Your day begins with a relaxed exploration of the Merzouga region, a unique desert landscape at the edge of the golden Erg Chebbi dunes:
- Hassi Labied Oasis – discover traditional Berber irrigation channels, still used today to cultivate crops in the desert.
- Merzouga Seasonal Lake – depending on the season, you may spot migratory birds such as flamingos.

- Khamlia Village – home of the Gnawa people, originally from sub-Saharan Africa, famous for their spiritual music and dance. Enjoy a live performance of Gnawa rhythms and a special “desert pizza” lunch baked in the sand.
- In the late afternoon, return to Merzouga where your camel caravan awaits. Ride gently across the dunes at sunset , watching the colors of the Sahara shift from gold to deep red.

Upon arrival at your camp, settle into your private tent and enjoy a traditional Berber dinner by the campfire, followed by local drumming and stargazing under one of the clearest skies in the world .
Overnight Camp Options
- Standard Desert Camp (included): Private tent with comfortable bedding; shared or private facilities depending on availability.
- Luxury Desert Camp (upgrade): Spacious en-suite tent with hot shower, electricity, stylish décor, and full comfort.
Supplement for Luxury Camp: +€80 per person

itinerary.title: Merzouga – Todra Gorge – Dades Gorge
body: Wake up early for a magical sunrise over the Erg Chebbi dunes , a breathtaking moment where the golden sands seem to glow in every direction. Afterward, your camel guide will lead you on a peaceful camel trek back across the dunes to your riad, giving you one last chance to admire the ever-changing colors of the desert.

Following a hearty breakfast, we depart for Tinghir and the spectacular Todra Gorge, one of Morocco’s natural wonders. These towering canyon walls, rising up to 300 meters, create a dramatic landscape perfect for a gentle walk along the riverbed or short hikes into the gorge.

After lunch in the gorge, we continue our journey through the Dades Valley, famous for its lush greenery, ancient kasbahs, and unusual rock formations known as the “Monkey Toes” . Along the way, you’ll see fortified villages and winding roads that make this valley one of Morocco’s most photogenic regions.
Overnight stay in a charming Moroccan-style hotel in the heart of the Dades Gorge, where you’ll enjoy dinner and a restful night surrounded by dramatic scenery.

itinerary.title: Dades Gorge – Ouarzazate – Aït Ben Haddou – Tizi N’Tichka Pass – Marrakech
body: After breakfast at your hotel, set off along the Dades Valley, following the famous “Road of a Thousand Kasbahs” . This route offers countless photo opportunities of ancient fortresses, Berber villages, and fertile valleys framed by the rugged Atlas Mountains.

Our first stop will be at Kalaat Mgouna , known as the “Valley of Roses”. Here you’ll have the chance to discover traditional rosewater products and perfumes, crafted by local cooperatives and cherished throughout Morocco.

Continuing on, we reach Ouarzazate , nicknamed the “Hollywood of Africa” for its role as a filming location for legendary movies and TV shows such as Gladiator, Lawrence of Arabia, and Game of Thrones.

The highlight of the day is a visit to the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Aït Ben Haddou Kasbah , the largest and most famous kasbah in Morocco. This fortified village of earthen clay architecture has stood for centuries and remains a living example of Morocco’s rich cultural heritage. After exploring its winding alleys and history, enjoy a leisurely lunch nearby.
In the afternoon, we cross the majestic Tizi n’Tichka Pass (2,260m) , the highest road in Morocco, winding through breathtaking mountain scenery, Berber hamlets, and terraced fields.
By early evening, we arrive in Marrakech , where your unforgettable 4-day desert adventure from Fes to Marrakech concludes with a drop-off at your riad or hotel.

tours.title: 5 Days 4×4 Adventure – Erg Chegaga Sahara Desert Experience

seo.title: 5 Days 4×4 Adventure – Erg Chegaga Sahara Desert Experience | Toubkal Peaks Travel Tours

summary: Embark on an unforgettable adventure from the bustling imperial city of Marrakech to the vast, golden dunes of Erg Chigaga. This 5-day journey combines Morocco’s spectacular mountain landscapes, historic kasbahs, lush river valleys, and the remote Sahara Desert. Traverse the High Atlas Mountains, cross the Draa Valley, explore traditional Berber villages, and spend a night under the stars in the desert — a true immersion into Moroccan culture and natural beauty.

itinerary.title: Marrakech → Ait Ben Haddou (≈180 km / 4 hrs)
body: Your journey begins with a morning pick-up from your hotel or riad in Marrakech. From the vibrant streets of the city, you will ascend into the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n’Tichka Pass (2,260 m), Morocco’s highest mountain road. Along the way, the scenery unfolds with terraced valleys, snow-capped peaks in winter, and small Berber villages clinging to the mountainsides.

Your first stop is Kasbah Telouet, an ancient palace of the powerful Glaoui family. Wander through the crumbling walls and beautifully carved doors while imagining the lives of Morocco’s historic elites. Continue to the UNESCO-listed Ait Ben Haddou, an iconic hilltop kasbah made of red clay, famously featured in films like Gladiator and Lawrence of Arabia. Explore the winding streets, climb to the panoramic viewpoints, and capture unforgettable photographs of the kasbah with the surrounding valley bathed in the afternoon light.
Spend the night in a traditional Moroccan-style hotel nearby, enjoying local cuisine and the calm of the Atlas foothills.
Meals: Breakfast & Dinner

itinerary.title: Ait Ben Haddou → Dades Valley (≈160 km / 3.5 hrs)
body: After breakfast, depart from Ait Ben Haddou and continue eastwards, crossing the rugged Sarhro Mountains. The landscape changes dramatically from the lush High Atlas to jagged volcanic peaks and deep gorges. You’ll notice the contrast of rocky terrain punctuated by abandoned kasbahs, silent witnesses to Morocco’s rich history.

As you approach the Draa Valley, Morocco’s longest river valley, the scenery softens into fertile green stretches dotted with palm groves, mud-brick villages, and traditional irrigation systems known as khettaras. Stop along the way to explore Berber villages, meet local families, and experience a glimpse of everyday life in rural Morocco. The valley offers incredible photography opportunities, especially at sunset when the golden light illuminates the palm groves and kasbahs.
Arrive in Zagora for an overnight stay, your gateway to the Sahara Desert.
Meals: Breakfast & Dinner

itinerary.title: Dades Valley → Todra Gorge → Nekob → Zagora (≈250 km / 5 hrs)
body: This morning begins with a visit to Todra Gorge, one of Morocco’s most impressive natural formations. Towering sandstone cliffs rise nearly 300 meters above the valley floor, creating narrow canyon paths ideal for short walks and photography.

Continue towards Nekob, a traditional Berber town with ancient kasbahs, local markets, and mud-brick architecture. Stroll through the town, interact with locals, and witness traditional crafts being made.

The drive back through the Draa Valley offers additional scenic viewpoints of palm groves, kasbahs, and small villages tucked along the valley floor. Each stop presents a perfect chance to photograph the contrast of desert landscapes against green oases. Arrive in Zagora in the late afternoon, where you can relax and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere of this desert gateway.
Meals: Breakfast & Dinner
Accommodation at: Traditional Moroccan style Hotel (Standard).

itinerary.title: Zagora → M’Hamid → Erg Chigaga (≈160 km / 5 hrs)
body: Today’s journey takes you deeper into the edge of the Sahara Desert. Begin with a stop at Tamgrout (Tamegroute), a village renowned for its green pottery. Witness Berber artisans creating distinctive green-glazed bowls, pots, and decorative items using traditional techniques. Don’t miss the 13th-century Koran library, an underground repository of ancient manuscripts, showcasing centuries of Moroccan Islamic scholarship.
Continue to M’Hamid, the last town before the expansive desert. Explore the palm groves and mud-brick houses while enjoying lunch and a taste of local life.
From M’Hamid, your 4×4 will traverse the wild desert landscapes, with occasional stops at small oases such as Oasis Sacré, a hidden water source amidst the arid plains.

Arrive at Erg Chigaga, where the vast golden dunes await. Enjoy a camel trek at sunset (~45 minutes) across the shifting sands, capturing the breathtaking colors of the desert as the sun dips below the horizon. Afterward, settle at your desert camp, experiencing traditional Berber hospitality and a night under the stars.
Meals: Breakfast & Dinner

itinerary.title: Erg Chigaga → Marrakech (≈421 km / 9 hrs)
body: Rise early to witness a desert sunrise, with the soft morning light transforming the dunes into golden waves. After breakfast, begin the return journey to Marrakech by 4×4, crossing the Paris-Dakar route, famous for its challenging sand dunes and rocky desert tracks.
Stop at Taznakht, a village renowned for its handmade Berber carpets. Watch weavers at work and shop for unique souvenirs.

As you ascend the High Atlas Mountains once again, enjoy panoramic views of rugged peaks and valleys before descending into Marrakech. Arrive in the city in the evening, completing a journey that spans mountains, valleys, and the vast Sahara Desert.
Meals: Breakfast

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Ouarzazate – Zagora
body: Meals: Dinner

Embark on a 3-day Erg Chigaga dunes adventure from Marrakech. You will be picked up from your hotel and begin the scenic drive through the Tizi n’Tichka pass at 2,260 meters in the High Atlas Mountains. Along the way, enjoy breathtaking landscapes, colorful valleys, and traditional Berber villages.

Your route takes you to Ait Benhaddou, a UNESCO-listed fortified ksar famous for its Kasbahs. This village has served as a backdrop for numerous films such as Lawrence of Arabia, Jesus of Nazareth, and Gladiator. Take a walk up to the hilltop for panoramic views of the town and surrounding desert landscapes.

Continue to Ouarzazate, where you will stop for lunch near the Kasbah of Taourirt. After lunch, drive south through volcanic mountains and Ait Saoun village, a historic caravan route for Sahara traders from Timbuktu.

Reach Agdez, the first administrative center of the Draa Valley, known for its lush palm groves and traditional kasbahs. Continue through the lunar-like landscapes of the pre-Sahara until you arrive in Zagora, a small town and the birthplace of the Saadian dynasty that ruled Morocco in the 17th century.
End the day with dinner at your hotel and overnight stay in a traditional Moroccan-style hotel.

itinerary.title: Zagora – Tamegroute – Mhamid – Off-road to Erg Chigaga Dunes
body: - Transport: ~4 hours (excluding off-road camel adventure)
- Meals: Breakfast & Dinner included
- Accommodation: Standard desert camp (Luxury camp optional at extra cost)
Morning Departure from Zagora:

After breakfast, leave the town of Zagora, historically an important trading hub on the caravan route to Timbuktu. The journey begins with scenic drives through the Draa Valley, dotted with palm groves , mud-brick kasbahs , and small Berber villages, offering a glimpse into traditional rural life.
Stop in Tamegroute:

Visit Tamegroute, a village renowned for its green pottery workshops , where artisans create beautiful handmade ceramics using traditional techniques. Explore the village and step into the historic Koranic library and school , one of the oldest in Morocco, housing thousands of ancient manuscripts. This stop provides a cultural insight into Islamic scholarship and local craft heritage.
Continue to M’Hamid / Lmhamid El Ghizlane:

Travel south through small desert towns like Tagnite toward M’Hamid, the last settlement before entering the Sahara. This area marks the beginning of the true desert landscape, with wide plains, acacia trees , and soft sand dunes. Here, your off-road adventure begins, crossing rugged pre-Sahara terrain in a 4×4 or guided vehicle, giving a sense of adventure before reaching the vast Erg Chigaga dunes.
Arrival at Erg Chigaga Dunes:

In the late afternoon, arrive at the Erg Chigaga dunes, some of the largest and most remote in Morocco . Mount your camel for a ride across the undulating golden sands and experience the breathtaking sunset over the dunes . The warm desert colors and endless horizon make this a perfect moment for photography and reflection.
Evening in the Desert Camp:

Spend the night in a traditional Berber tent or upgrade to a luxury desert camp . Dinner is served under the stars, accompanied by the peaceful sounds of the desert and optional Berber music . This overnight stay offers a unique chance to experience the serenity and magic of the Sahara, far from city lights.

itinerary.title: Chegaga – Iriki – Foum Zguid – Tazenakht – Atlas Mountain – Marrakech
body: - Transport: ~8–9 hours (with stops for sightseeing and photography)
- Meals: Breakfast included
Morning Departure from Erg Chigaga:

After enjoying a sunrise in the desert and a traditional breakfast at your camp, depart from Erg Chigaga. The morning drive begins through pre-Sahara landscapes, featuring rolling dunes, acacia trees , and wide-open plains that give a sense of the Sahara’s vastness.
Iriki Lake Stop:

Your route passes Iriki Lake , once a seasonal lake and now a protected natural reserve. This area attracts migratory birds and other wildlife. It’s a great spot to take photographs of the desert ecosystem and enjoy a quiet moment surrounded by peaceful desert scenery.
Foum Zguid Town:

Continue to Foum Zguid, a small desert town that historically served as a trading post for caravans crossing the pre-Sahara. Here, you can glimpse traditional Berber life and see the blend of desert culture and modern Moroccan settlements.
Tazenakht Carpet Village:

Next, visit Tazenakht, famous for its traditional Berber carpets and weaving workshops . This town is one of Morocco’s largest carpet production centers. Guests can observe artisans at work and purchase high-quality carpets directly from local workshops, learning about the intricate patterns and symbolism in Berber weaving.
Crossing the High Atlas Mountains:

As you continue north, cross the High Atlas Mountains again . The route offers dramatic scenery with winding roads, rugged cliffs, and lush valleys, contrasting sharply with the desert landscapes you saw earlier. itinerary.title: Marrakech – High Atlas – Aït Benhaddou – Ouarzazate – Skoura – Roses Valley – Dades Valley
body: Meals: Dinner included

After breakfast, your driver will pick you up from your hotel/riad in Marrakech . Travel through the High Atlas Mountains along the winding road of the Tizi n’Tichka Pass (2,260m), where you’ll enjoy breathtaking panoramas and stops for photos.
Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Kasbah Aït Benhaddou , Morocco’s most famous fortress village. Explore its narrow alleys, mud-brick kasbahs, and climb to the top for sweeping desert views .

Continue to Ouarzazate , known as the “Hollywood of Africa,” with its Atlas Film Studios and Taourirt Kasbah. Drive through the Skoura palm oasis and the Valley of Roses , renowned for rosewater distilleries and cosmetics.
Arrive at the spectacular Dades Valley , carved by the river and lined with red & ochre cliffs. Dinner and overnight in a Moroccan-style hotel in the Valley.

itinerary.title: Dades Gorge – Todra Gorge – Erfoud – Merzouga Desert
body: Meals: Breakfast & Dinner included

After breakfast, enjoy the stunning drive along the Road of 1000 Kasbahs , dotted with ancient fortresses. Stop at the Todra Gorge , where sheer cliffs rise up to 300m — a favorite for climbers and hikers. Take a short walk by the river.

Continue via Erfoud , famous for its fossil workshops and dates festival. The scenery gradually transforms into golden dunes as you approach Merzouga Desert , home to the magnificent Erg Chebbi dunes.
Settle into your desert riad/hotel facing the dunes. Relax, watch the dunes change colors at sunset , and enjoy a traditional Berber dinner.

itinerary.title: Merzouga Desert Exploration – Khamlia Village – Camel Ride – Sahara Camp
body: Distance: ~40 km local exploration
Travel Time: 3–4 hrs of easy driving (with visits)
Camel Ride: ~1 hr each way (sunset & sunrise)
Meals: Breakfast & Dinner included
Day Highlights
Your day begins with a relaxed exploration of the Merzouga region, a unique desert landscape at the edge of the golden Erg Chebbi dunes:
- Hassi Labied Oasis – discover traditional Berber irrigation channels, still used today to cultivate crops in the desert.
- Merzouga Seasonal Lake – depending on the season, you may spot migratory birds such as flamingos.

- Khamlia Village – home of the Gnawa people, originally from sub-Saharan Africa, famous for their spiritual music and dance. Enjoy a live performance of Gnawa rhythms and a special “desert pizza” lunch baked in the sand.
- In the late afternoon, return to Merzouga where your camel caravan awaits. Ride gently across the dunes at sunset , watching the colors of the Sahara shift from gold to deep red.

Upon arrival at your camp, settle into your private tent and enjoy a traditional Berber dinner by the campfire, followed by local drumming and stargazing under one of the clearest skies in the world .

- Luxury Desert Camp (upgrade): Spacious en-suite tent with hot shower, electricity, stylish décor, and full comfort.

itinerary.title: Merzouga – Ziz Valley – Midelt – Azrou – Fes
body: Meals: Breakfast

After enjoying a hearty breakfast in Merzouga, we leave the desert behind and begin the journey back to Fes, one of Morocco’s most iconic imperial cities. The road winds through the breathtaking Ziz Valley, a fertile oasis dotted with palm groves, kasbahs, and small Berber villages. Take time to pause and capture the panoramic views of this unique desert landscape, where the contrast between green palms and golden cliffs is truly stunning.

As we ascend into the High Atlas Mountains, the scenery transforms dramatically: rugged peaks, winding roads, and traditional Berber villages clinging to the hillsides. We stop in the town of Midelt, a lively market town nestled between the Middle and High Atlas ranges, where you can enjoy a relaxed lunch and perhaps browse local crafts.

Our journey continues through Azrou, a town famous for its cedar forests. These ancient forests are home to the playful Barbary monkeys, and you’ll have the chance to see them in their natural habitat—an unforgettable wildlife experience.

Passing through Ifrane, often called “Little Switzerland” for its alpine-style architecture and clean streets, we descend toward Fes. You’ll notice the striking contrast between the mountain landscapes and the historic city that awaits. By early evening, around 5:00 PM, we arrive in Fes, where your next adventure in Morocco’s cultural heart will begin.
Total journey: Approximately 7 hours

summary: Immerse yourself in the stunning landscapes of the High Atlas Mountains on our 2-Day Azzaden Trek. This trek takes you through traditional Berber villages, lush valleys, and scenic mountain passes, offering an authentic cultural and trekking experience just a short distance from Marrakech.

Experience the majestic beauty of the High Atlas Mountains at Toubkal National Park, spanning 36,000 hectares and home to Morocco’s highest peak, Jbel Toubkal (4,167 m). Located just 63 km south of Marrakech, the park is a haven for trekkers, climbers, and nature enthusiasts seeking breathtaking landscapes and unforgettable mountain adventures.

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Imi Oughlad – Tizi Oussem
itinerary.accommodation: Panoramic Berber Guesthouse in Tizi Oussem
body: After breakfast, we depart Marrakech by minibus or 4×4 , journeying from the plains into the heart of the High Atlas Mountains . We arrive at Imi Oughlad, where we meet our experienced muleteers and their mules to carry luggage and supplies.

From Imi Oughlad, we embark on a scenic 4–5 hour trek . The route ascends to the Tacht Pass (2,000 m) , offering panoramic views of the surrounding mountains and valleys. From the pass, we descend into the lush Azaden Valley , a journey combining breathtaking scenery with a moderate trekking challenge.

We stop for a traditional lunch in Imi Nifri, enjoying authentic local dishes before continuing the trek to Tizi Oussem , a traditional Berber village nestled in the valley. Here, we spend the night at a panoramic Berber guesthouse , with stunning mountain views. Dinner is served at the guesthouse, completing a day rich in natural beauty and cultural experiences.

itinerary.title: Tizi Oussem – Imlil – Marrakech

body: After breakfast, we continue our trek, passing through scenic juniper forests on the ascent to Tizi Mzik (2,269 m) . Here, we pause to enjoy a picnic lunch near Azib Berdoun, taking in the spectacular mountain views.

Following lunch, we descend toward Imlil (1,750 m) , a charming village in the Mizane Valley often referred to as the “small Chamonix” of Morocco. Imlil is a major trekking hub, where many treks to Toubkal begin. This marks the end of your trek, where you will say farewell to your guide and muleteers, celebrating the memories and achievements of your High Atlas adventure.

Along the way, your cook will prepare a picnic lunch in the open air, giving you a chance to savor local flavors while surrounded by mountains and fresh alpine air.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Marrakech – Transfer to Imlil (Riad Berber Towers)
body: - Transfer time: ~1.5 hrs (65 km)
- Start point: Marrakech (hotel/riad or airport)
- End point: Imlil (1,740m, High Atlas)
- Accommodation: Riad Berber Towers, Imlil
- Meals included: Dinner

Your adventure begins with a warm welcome at Marrakech Airport or pick-up from your hotel/riad in Marrakech. After meeting your driver, you’ll set off south towards the High Atlas Mountains, leaving behind the bustling medina and entering the tranquil countryside.

The scenic drive (approx. 1.5 hours / 65 km) takes you through winding roads, olive groves, and traditional Berber villages, with the mountains rising dramatically in the distance. As you climb higher into the foothills of the Atlas, you’ll notice the air becoming fresher and cooler.

By late afternoon, you’ll arrive in Imlil (1,740m), the main trailhead for treks in Toubkal National Park. Nestled in a lush valley surrounded by walnut and cherry trees, Imlil is often called the “Chamonix of Morocco.”

Here, you’ll settle into your accommodation at the authentic Riad Berber Towers, where you’ll be greeted with traditional Moroccan hospitality. Enjoy a refreshing welcome tea on the terrace with panoramic views of the surrounding peaks and villages.

In the evening, savor a homemade Berber dinner, prepared with local ingredients, before resting overnight in the peaceful setting of your riad. This night in Imlil allows you to acclimatize gently to the altitude and mountain environment, preparing you for the hikes ahead.

itinerary.title: Hike to Tizi n’Mzik Pass – Return to Riad Berber Towers
body: - Hiking distance: ~10–12 km (round trip)
- Duration: 5–6 hrs
- Elevation gain/loss: +750m / –750m
- Highest point: Tizi n’Mzik Pass (2,489m)
- Meals included: Breakfast, Picnic Lunch, Dinner
- Accommodation: Riad Berber Towers, Imlil

After a hearty breakfast on the terrace of Riad Berber Towers, your mountain guide will meet you to start today’s adventure. The hike begins right from the doorstep of the riad, taking you through the charming alleyways of Imlil and out into the walnut groves and terraced fields where local Berber families farm apples, cherries, and barley.

The trail soon climbs steadily on a mule path, zig-zagging above the valley with ever-widening views. As you ascend, the scenery changes from cultivated terraces to alpine slopes dotted with juniper and wild herbs. With each step, the air grows fresher and the panoramas more dramatic.

By late morning, you’ll reach the Tizi n’Mzik Pass (2,489m), a high mountain saddle with sweeping views down into the colorful Azzaden Valley on one side and back toward the Imlil Valley on the other. On clear days, you may even spot some of the higher snow-capped summits of the Atlas Range in the distance.

Here, your cook and muleteer will prepare a freshly made picnic lunch in nature, often featuring local bread, salads, tagine, and mint tea. This is the perfect place to rest, take photos, and breathe in the silence of the mountains.

In the afternoon, you’ll descend along the same path, taking time to enjoy the changing light on the mountains and perhaps stopping to greet shepherds or villagers along the way. By mid to late afternoon, you’ll return to Riad Berber Towers, where mint tea will be waiting for you on the panoramic terrace.

The rest of the day is for relaxation — watch the sunset over the surrounding peaks, explore Imlil village, or simply unwind before dinner. In the evening, enjoy a delicious Berber-style dinner prepared with seasonal ingredients before settling in for another cozy night in the riad.
Overnight at Riad Berber Towers, Imlil.

itinerary.title: Hike to Sidi Chamharouch – Picnic Lunch by the River & Waterfalls
body: - Hiking distance: ~8–10 km (round trip)
- Duration: 4–5 hrs
- Elevation gain/loss: +450m / –450m
- Highest point: Sidi Chamharouch (2,310m)
- Meals included: Breakfast, Picnic Lunch, Dinner
- Accommodation: Riad Berber Towers, Imlil

After breakfast at Riad Berber Towers, you’ll set out with your guide on a beautiful day hike that blends nature, spirituality, and local culture. The trail begins gently, following the path through the Mizane Valley, crossing small Berber hamlets with stone-built houses and terraced fields of barley and corn.

As you ascend gradually, the landscape becomes more rugged, with juniper bushes, grazing goats, and the sound of rushing streams accompanying your journey. After about 2 hours, you will reach the shrine of Sidi Chamharouch (2,310m), known as the “King of the Jinn”. This white-painted shrine is an important pilgrimage site for Moroccans, where locals come seeking blessings and healing. The area also marks the spiritual gateway to Mount Toubkal.

Nearby, your cook and muleteer will prepare a freshly made picnic lunch beside the river and waterfalls, a peaceful setting perfect for resting, refreshing your feet in the cold water, and soaking in the mountain atmosphere.

After lunch, you’ll retrace your steps down the valley, enjoying the afternoon light on the surrounding peaks and villages. Returning to Riad Berber Towers, relax with mint tea on the terrace before a hearty Berber dinner.
Overnight at Riad Berber Towers, Imlil.

itinerary.title: Hike in Ouirgane Valley – Salt Mines & Jewish Heritage – Lunch with a Berber Family – Return to Marrakech
body: - Transfer time: Imlil → Ouirgane ~1 hr | Ouirgane → Marrakech ~1.5 hrs
- Hiking distance: ~6–8 km
- Duration: 2–3 hrs (easy/moderate hike)
- Elevation: 1,000–1,200m (gentle valley walk)
- Meals included: Breakfast, Lunch
- Accommodation: Not included (end of trip)

After breakfast at Riad Berber Towers, you’ll meet your driver and guide and head to the Ouirgane Valley, known as the “Garden of the Atlas” for its fertile fields, red-earth hills, olive groves, and walnut trees.
Your day’s hike takes you through peaceful landscapes, pine forests, and Berber villages. Along the way, you will explore three unique cultural highlights:

- Traditional Salt Mines – still worked by local families, where mineral-rich water evaporates in shallow pans to form gleaming crystals. Salt from Ouirgane was once a prized trading good and even used as currency.

- Jewish Heritage – Ouirgane was once home to a vibrant Jewish community. You may visit the remains of the old Jewish synagogue and cemetery, silent witnesses to centuries of coexistence and trade in the valley. This gives the hike a deeper historical dimension, connecting Berber and Jewish traditions of the Atlas.
- Berber Family Lunch – you’ll be warmly welcomed into a local home to enjoy a freshly prepared lunch of tagine, olives, homemade bread, and mint tea.
After lunch, your driver will take you back across the Atlas foothills, arriving in Marrakech by late afternoon.
End of trip – a day blending nature, history, and authentic hospitality.

itinerary.title: Marrakech → Aguersioual → Matat → Id Issa → Ouaougmout
body: - Transfer: Marrakech → Aguersioual (1,600 m) ~1h30 drive
- Hike distance: ~12 km / 7.5 miles
- Hiking time: 5–6 hrs
- Elevation gain: +600 m / Elevation loss: –350 m
- Start altitude: Aguersioual – 1,600 m
- Highest point: Tizi Oudid – 2,200 m
- Overnight: Ouaougmout Village – 1,850 m

Morning transfer: After breakfast in Marrakech, your driver will take you south through the foothills of the High Atlas. Along the way, you’ll see fertile valleys, villages of flat-roofed houses, and views of snow-capped peaks in the distance. Arrive at Aguersioual (1,600 m), the trailhead where you meet your muleteer and begin the trek.

Hike: The trail winds gently uphill through juniper forests and terraced fields, with stops to greet friendly Berber farmers. You’ll pass through Matat village, with its walnut and apple orchards, before reaching the Id Issa Valley — a lush valley surrounded by red-earth slopes.
Lunch: Pause at the panoramic Tizi Oudid Pass (2,200 m). Enjoy a freshly prepared picnic lunch while overlooking the valleys of Matat and Id Issa.
Afternoon: Continue along mule paths past small hamlets, waving to children playing in the fields. The path descends into the green valley of Ouaougmout (1,850 m).
Evening: Settle into a Berber family house. Expect a warm welcome, mint tea, and a traditional dinner of tagine or couscous.

itinerary.title: Ouaougmout → Tiziane → Talat N’Ikiss → Assaka → Tizgui n’Tkente
body: - Hike distance: ~14 km / 8.5 miles
- Hiking time: 6–7 hrs
- Elevation gain: +650 m / Elevation loss: –450 m
- Start altitude: Ouaougmout – 1,850 m
- Highest point: Talat N’Ikiss – ~2,200 m
- Overnight: Tizgui n’Tkente – 1,900 m
Morning hike: Leave Ouaougmout and walk through fields of barley and almond groves. The trail takes you through Tiziane village, where you may see women baking bread in communal ovens.

Scenery: As you climb towards Talat N’Ikiss Valley, the landscape changes into wild, rugged hills dotted with juniper trees. The red soil contrasts beautifully with green terraces — a classic Atlas panorama.
Lunch: Stop in the peaceful Assaka village, where your cook prepares a picnic under the shade of walnut trees. Enjoy the quietness of rural life far from modern distractions.
Afternoon: Continue along shepherd trails to Tizgui n’Tkente (1,900 m). This remote village has stone-built houses perched on a hillside and offers stunning sunset views.
Evening: Stay in a Berber guesthouse. Share dinner with your hosts, and if you’re lucky, listen to traditional Berber songs by the fireplace.

itinerary.title: Tizgui → Azib Assoul → Tizi N’Tagdalt → Tizi Oussem
body: - Hike distance: ~15 km / 9 miles
- Hiking time: 6–7 hrs
- Elevation gain: +800 m / Elevation loss: –950 m
- Start altitude: Tizgui – 1,900 m
- Highest point: Tizi N’Tagdalt – 2,700 m
- Overnight: Tizi Oussem – 1,850 m
Morning: Begin the day trekking through alpine meadows where shepherds graze their flocks. You’ll pass by Azib Assoul, a seasonal pasture where Berber families bring animals in summer.
Climb: Gradual ascent to the Tizi N’Tagdalt Pass (2,700 m), the highest point of the trek. The panoramic view reveals the vast Azzaden Valley below and the jagged ridges of the High Atlas.
Lunch: Picnic at or near the pass, surrounded by mountain silence and sweeping views.
Afternoon descent: The trail leads downhill into the fertile Azzaden Valley, lined with walnut groves, terraced fields, and stone villages.
Evening: Arrive in Tizi Oussem (1,850 m). Your host family welcomes you with mint tea on the terrace. Dinner is typically a hearty vegetable tagine prepared with produce from the valley.

itinerary.title: Tizi Oussem → Tizi Mzik → Imlil → Marrakech
body: Morning climb: After breakfast, begin the ascent to the Tizi Mzik Pass (2,489 m). The path offers dramatic views back over the Azzaden Valley and across to Imlil.
Optional extension (2 hrs): If energy allows, detour to Azib Tamsoult and the spectacular Ighouliden Waterfalls, a hidden gem cascading into rocky pools.
Lunch: Picnic in Azib Berdoun, under walnut trees beside a flowing stream.
Final stretch: Continue down into the famous trekking hub of Imlil (1,740 m), a lively village at the foot of Mount Toubkal.
Afternoon transfer: Meet your driver for the return to Marrakech (~1h 30m), arriving late afternoon.
End of trek — carrying memories of mountain passes, Berber hospitality, and timeless landscapes.

itinerary.title: Marrakech → Moulay Brahim Gorges → Asni → Imi Oughlad → Gliz
body: Your adventure begins with a morning transfer from bustling Marrakech (450 m) into the foothills of the Atlas. You’ll drive through the winding Moulay Brahim Gorges and the lively town of Asni (1,150 m), famous for its weekly Saturday Berber market.

On arrival at Imi Oughlad (1,450 m), you’ll meet your local muleteer crew and set off on your first hike. The trail climbs steadily through pine, juniper, and terraced farmlands to Tizi N’Elbour Pass (1,700 m). From here, enjoy sweeping views of the valleys below. Continue through tiny hamlets like Imsker and Tinghar, before descending gently to Gliz village (1,650 m).
Picnic lunch en route under walnut or pine trees.
Dinner with a Berber family offers your first taste of Atlas hospitality.
Hiking: 4–5 hrs | Ascent: +500 m | Descent: -250 m
Overnight in a Berber family house in Gliz.

itinerary.title: Gliz → Amssakrou → Tizi N’Ougrssioual → Matat
body: Today’s trek takes you through some of the most beautiful farmlands in the region. Walk along walnut groves and terraced fields in Amssakrou Valley, following shepherd paths that link remote villages.
Picnic lunch along the trail near riverside fields.
The highlight is the climb to Tizi N’Ougrssioual Pass (2,000 m), where the red clay villages of the Azzaden Valley come into view against the backdrop of snow-capped peaks.
After descending into the valley, stop for lunch near Agrssioual village before continuing to Matat (1,800 m).
Dinner in a guest house, with hearty tagine and fresh bread baked in a clay oven.
Hiking: 5–6 hrs | Ascent: +400 m | Descent: -500 m
Overnight in a Berber guest house in Matat.

itinerary.title: Matat → Tizi Oudid → Id Issa → Tizi Oussem → Azib Tamsoult
body: After breakfast, climb gradually towards Tizi Oudid Pass (2,200 m), a balcony with magnificent views of the High Atlas. Descend through juniper forests and traditional Berber hamlets to reach Id Issa village.

Continue deeper into the Azzaden Valley, known for its dramatic red-earth landscapes and walnut groves. Pass through Tizi Oussem (1,850 m), one of the valley’s largest villages, before reaching Azib Tamsoult (2,250 m),Lunch with views of terraced walnut groves. a summer pasture hamlet where shepherds graze their flocks.
Enjoy a hot meal in the evening surrounded by high peaks.
Hiking: 6 hrs | Ascent: +700 m | Descent: -400 m
Overnight in Refuge Tamsoult (2,250 m).

itinerary.title: Azib Tamsoult → Ighouliden Waterfalls → Tizi Mzik → Imlil
body: A spectacular day! Begin with a short hike to the Ighouliden waterfalls (2,400 m), cascading down rocky cliffs – one of the most beautiful spots in the Atlas. From here, climb steadily to Tizi Mzik Pass (2,489 m), Picnic lunch at the pass or during descent. offering panoramic views of the Azzaden and Imlil valleys.
Descend on mule tracks lined with juniper and wildflowers until you reach Imlil (1,750 m), the main trailhead village of the High Atlas.
A traditional dinner awaits you at Riad Berber Towers, with warm Berber hospitality.
Hiking: 6–7 hrs | Ascent: +600 m | Descent: -950 m
Overnight at Riad Berber Towers, Imlil.

The trail climbs steadily along the Mizane Valley, passing streams, walnut groves, and views of Mount Toubkal (4,167 m).
Have a picnic lunch by the river before descending back to Imlil.
Hiking: 4–5 hrs | Ascent: +600 m | Descent: -600 m
Overnight at Riad Berber Towers, Imlil.

Lunch with a Berber family, tasting freshly baked bread, olive oil, and homegrown vegetables.
Afternoon transfer back to Marrakech (~1.5 hrs).
Arrival in the early evening, with memories of valleys, villages, and waterfalls.
Hiking: 2–3 hrs | Easy walk

tours.title: 7 Days Jbel Saghro-Trekking – Morocco’s Rugged Desert Mountains

seo.title: 7 Days Jbel Saghro-Trekking – Morocco’s Rugged Desert Mountains | Toubkal Peaks Travel Tours

summary: Jbel Saghro is a dramatic mountain range nestled between the High Atlas and the Sahara Desert, offering landscapes that are both rugged and mesmerizing. From jagged volcanic peaks and deep gorges to expansive plateaus and rock formations sculpted by centuries of wind and erosion, the scenery is truly unique.

The region is home to the semi-nomadic Aït Atta Berbers, whose enduring traditions and warm hospitality bring a rich cultural dimension to every journey. Unlike the snow-capped High Atlas, Saghro enjoys a mild climate, making it an ideal trekking destination during winter and early spring.

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Tichka Pass – Tagudilt Village
body: Distance/Travel: ~430 km / 9 hrs
Highlights:
- Tichka Pass (2,260 m) : The highest road pass in Morocco, offering panoramic views of the High Atlas peaks and deep valleys. A spectacular introduction to Morocco’s mountainous landscapes.
- Berber Villages : Small settlements along the route where locals live in mud-brick houses and practice traditional farming. A glimpse into daily life in the Atlas.
- Ouarzazate : Known as the “Gateway to the Sahara,” with its historic kasbahs and film studios where blockbusters like Gladiator were filmed.
- Skoura Oasis : A lush valley with palm groves and ancient kasbahs, showcasing the contrast between desert and fertile land.
- Klaa El Mgouna : Famous for roses and rosewater production. A lovely spot to stop for lunch and explore local crafts.
- Boumalne Dades : Edge of the Dades Valley, dramatic cliffs, and winding roads known as the “Road of a Thousand Kasbahs.”
- Tagudilt Village : A quiet Berber village where we meet our mule team. Authentic experience of mountain village life.

itinerary.title: Tagudilt – Azarzim Pass – Almou N’Ouarg
body: Trekking Distance: ~14 km / 6 hrs
Highlights:
- High Plateau Trek : Wide-open spaces with panoramic desert-like views, scattered with rocks and wild plants.
- Azarzim Pass : Offers a sweeping view over the Saghro mountains and surrounding valleys; perfect spot for photos.
- Rock Formations : Unique volcanic shapes sculpted by wind and erosion, giving the landscape a surreal feel.
- Azib Almou N’Ouarg : Traditional shepherds’ home where we camp and experience authentic nomadic life.

itinerary.title: Almou N’Ouarg – Summit of Jbel Saghro – Igli
body: Trekking Distance: ~18 km / 7.5 hrs
Highlights:
- Jbel Saghro Summit (Kouaouch, 2,592 m) : Spectacular panoramic views of the Saghro range, valleys, and desert plains beyond. A sense of accomplishment at the top!
- Tassigdelt Village : Small Berber village for lunch. Traditional mud-brick houses and local farming demonstrate daily life in Saghro.
- Igli Village : Nestled among almond orchards, Igli offers a peaceful setting and encounters with semi-nomadic families. A chance to see local customs and hospitality.

itinerary.title: Igli – Bab N’Ali
body: Trekking Distance: ~16 km / 7 hrs
Highlights:
- Almond Groves & Palm Trees : Fertile areas where locals grow almonds and dates, creating a contrast with the rocky surroundings.
- Nomadic Encounters : Shepherds and their families live in tents or small homes, moving seasonally with livestock.
- Bab N’Ali Village : Traditional village tucked in a valley, surrounded by desert and mountains. Camping here offers a quiet night under the stars.
- Valleys & Gorges : Dramatic sandstone cliffs carved by centuries of wind and water.

itinerary.title: Bab N’Ali – Asif Nirrazzoun

- River Valley Trek : Follow the flowing waters of Asif N’Irrrezzoun, with occasional natural pools.
- Irrezzoun N’Imlas : Picnic stop in a scenic valley with farms and wildflowers.
- Almond & Fig Orchards : Traditional cultivation by locals.
- Palm Groves : Lush greenery in an otherwise arid region, providing shade and beauty.
- Wildlife : Birds and desert animals occasionally spotted along the valley.

itinerary.title: Asif Nirrazzoun – Handour Village
body: Trekking Distance: ~10 km / 4 hrs
Highlights:
- Small Berber Villages : Pass through settlements with mud-brick houses and observe local crafts like weaving.
- Handour Village : A charming old village with cobbled streets, kasbah ruins, and friendly locals.
- Cultural Experience : Take a shower, wash clothes, stroll around, and enjoy traditional Berber dishes.

- Tichka Pass : Marvel again at the High Atlas mountains as we descend toward Marrakech.
- Marrakech Arrival : Return to the vibrant city, completing a diverse trek of mountains, desert, culture, and history.

tours.title: 7 Days Jbel Sirwa Trek

seo.title: 7 Days Jbel Sirwa Trek | Toubkal Peaks Travel Tours

summary: Explore the hidden gem of Morocco with a trek to Jbel Sirwa, a spectacular volcanic peak in the Anti-Atlas Mountains. Rising to 3,304 meters, this remote mountain offers dramatic landscapes, high-altitude plateaus, and breathtaking views of the surrounding High Atlas and the distant Sahara foothills.

Along the way, discover traditional Berber villages, interact with nomadic shepherds, and experience the untouched beauty of Morocco’s wilderness. Perfect for adventurers seeking a unique trekking experience, Jbel Sirwa combines volcanic terrain, panoramic vistas, and cultural immersion into one unforgettable journey.

itinerary.title: Marrakech → Tamllakout (1,800–1,900m)
body: Transfer: 4–5 hrs (≈220 km)
Meals: Dinner

Depart Marrakech in the morning and drive through the High Atlas Mountains, passing winding valleys, terraced fields, and small Berber villages. On the way, stop at scenic viewpoints to photograph snow-capped peaks and river valleys. Arrive in Tamllakout, a quiet Berber village at the foothills of Jbel Sirwa. Check into a guesthouse, enjoy a warm welcome with traditional mint tea, and savor a Moroccan dinner. The night allows for acclimatization and rest before trekking begins.
Highlights: Berber village, mint tea hospitality, High Atlas scenery.

Elevation Gain: +550 m
Hiking Time: 5–6 hrs

Begin trekking from Tamllakout, winding through quiet valleys, terraced fields, and small hamlets. Observe local Berber families tending goats and crops along the way. The trail gradually climbs, revealing dramatic volcanic peaks and basalt ridges in the distance. Pause for a picnic lunch surrounded by the highland scenery. Continue to Azib Mgist, a nomadic summer pasture, where you’ll set up camp. Enjoy a peaceful evening under the stars, listening to the sounds of nature.
Highlights: Nomadic life, volcanic valleys, starlit camping.

itinerary.title: Azib Mgist → Tissili Plateau (2,600m)
body: Hiking Distance: 14 km
Elevation Gain: +250 m
Hiking Time: 5–6 hrs
Meals: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

Today, trek across vast volcanic landscapes with basalt ridges, lava flows, and highland plateaus. The path is remote and quiet, offering a feeling of true wilderness. You may see nomadic shepherds and their flocks, goats grazing, and seasonal Berber gardens. Stop for a lunch break with panoramic views of surrounding peaks. Arrive at the Tissili Plateau, a remote area with dramatic rock formations and open skies. Camp overnight, enjoying a quiet, starlit night far from modern distractions.
Highlights: Remote volcanic terrain, Tissili Plateau, nomadic life.

itinerary.title: Tissili Plateau → Summit of Jbel Sirwa (3,304m) → Azib Iriri
body: Hiking Distance: 16 km
Elevation Gain: +700 m / Descent −1,000 m
Hiking Time: 6–7 hrs
Meals: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

Early morning, set off for the summit of Jbel Sirwa (3,304m). The ascent involves moderate climbing with rocky terrain, suitable for trekkers with good fitness. At the summit, enjoy 360° panoramic views of the High Atlas, Anti-Atlas, and even the Sahara foothills in the distance. After celebrating at the peak, descend to Azib Iriri, a nomadic pasture surrounded by volcanic peaks, and set up camp. Enjoy a campfire dinner and the peaceful night in nature.
Highlights: Summit of Jbel Sirwa, panoramic views, volcanic landscapes, camping under stars.

itinerary.title: Azib Iriri – Takshost
