tours.title: 8 Days Skiing in Morocco’s High Atlas

seo.title: 8 Days Skiing in Morocco’s High Atlas | Toubkal Peaks Travel Tours

summary: The High Atlas Mountains are not only Morocco’s highest range but also one of the most unique places in the world to enjoy ski touring. With Mount Toubkal standing at 4,167m, North Africa’s highest peak, the region offers an incredible playground for skiers seeking both adventure and culture.

From February to April, the snow conditions are at their best, transforming the rugged High Atlas valleys into a pristine ski terrain. Long, sweeping descents, dramatic alpine scenery, and challenging ascents make this a true skier’s paradise.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Marrakech – Gateway to the High Atlas
body: Welcome to Morocco! Upon arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport, you’ll be met by our driver and transferred to your charming riad in the old medina. The rest of the day is free to stroll through the maze-like souks, admire the colorful spice stalls, and soak in the energy of Jemaa el-Fna square, where storytellers, snake charmers, and food vendors come alive at sunset. This first evening is all about relaxation and preparing yourself for the mountain adventure ahead.
- Overnight in Marrakech

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Imlil – Trek to Toubkal Refuge (3,207m)
body: After breakfast, we leave the bustle of Marrakech behind and drive into the High Atlas Mountains (1h30). At Imlil village (1,740m), we meet our local muleteers who will carry luggage, leaving us free to ascend with skis and light packs.

The skinning begins gently through Berber villages and terraced fields, before entering the wilder Mizane Valley. A stop at the Chamharouch shrine (2,310m)—a spiritual site visited by pilgrims—offers a cultural glimpse. From here, the path climbs steadily, snow becoming deeper as we approach the alpine world. By afternoon we reach the Toubkal Refuge (3,207m), nestled beneath steep cliffs. Here, hot tea and a warm dinner await.
- 5–6 hrs trek / +1,467m ascent
- Overnight at Toubkal Refuge

itinerary.title: Ski Ascent of Mount Toubkal (4,167m)
body: Today we tackle North Africa’s highest peak. An early start allows us to skin up the south cwm, zig-zagging through snowy slopes. The climb is steady but demanding at altitude.

Reaching the summit cross of Toubkal (4,167m) is a thrilling moment—panoramic views stretch across the entire Atlas chain, with the Sahara Desert shimmering to the south. After a well-earned rest, comes the highlight: a long ski descent back to the refuge, weaving turns down wide open slopes.
- 6–7 hrs / +960m ascent / –960m descent
- Overnight at Toubkal Refuge

itinerary.title: Ski Ascent of Ras & Timesguida Ouanoukrim (4,083m & 4,089m)
body: We venture west towards the Ouanoukrim massif, home to the second- and third-highest peaks in North Africa. Using skins and sometimes crampons for steeper sections, we climb towards Ras (4,083m) and Timesguida (4,089m).
The ridge here offers dramatic alpine scenery, with jagged peaks and plunging valleys. From the summits, the reward is an exhilarating ski descent back to the refuge, carving turns in the fresh snow.
- 6 hrs / +900m ascent / –900m descent
- Overnight at Toubkal Refuge

itinerary.title: Ski Ascent of Akioud (4,030m)
body: Today’s target is Akioud Peak, a quieter but equally rewarding summit. The climb takes us through remote slopes, sometimes narrow couloirs, before opening onto wide, ski-friendly terrain.
The descent is a highlight of the trip, combining technical sections with sweeping runs. Back at the refuge, the group can relax over mint tea and hearty mountain food.
- 5–6 hrs / +820m ascent / –820m descent
- Overnight at Toubkal Refuge

itinerary.title: Tizi n’Ouanoums (3,670m) & Secret Valleys
body: This day is reserved for exploration. We skin up to the Tizi n’Ouanoums Pass (3,670m), a natural gateway into hidden valleys of the High Atlas. Depending on snow and weather, we may ski technical couloirs or explore untouched bowls.
It’s a day of discovery, often with few other skiers in sight—just the silence of the mountains and the crunch of skis on snow.
- 5 hrs / +500–700m ascent & descent
- Overnight at Toubkal Refuge

itinerary.title: Final Descent – Refuge to Imlil – Marrakech
body: After days of high peaks, it’s time for one last descent. From the refuge, we enjoy a long ski run down to Imlil, passing once again through alpine valleys and Berber hamlets.
At Imlil, we say goodbye to our mule team and transfer back to Marrakech (1h30). The afternoon is free for hammam baths, souvenir shopping, or a celebratory dinner overlooking the bustling square.
- 4–5 hrs descent
- Overnight in Marrakech

seo.title: 2 Days Mount Toubkal Trek | Toubkal Peaks Travel Tours

summary: This challenging 2-day trek takes you to the summit of Jebel Toubkal, the highest peak in North Africa. Perfect for fit and adventurous hikers, this trek requires no mountaineering experience, yet offers a demanding and rewarding climb. Enjoy spectacular panoramic views from the summit, then return to Marrakech in time to explore the city’s vibrant culture.

At 4,167 m, Mount Toubkal is the highest peak in North Africa. Our 2-Day Toubkal Trek is a challenging yet accessible adventure that requires no prior mountaineering experience, making it ideal for fit and enthusiastic hikers.

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Toubkal Refuge
body: After a transfer to the picturesque village of Imlil , we begin our trek along the scenic Mizane Valley . The trail first passes through the village of Aremd, then leads to the sacred shrine of Sidi Chamarouch , a site visited by both pilgrims and tourists.

Continuing east, the route crosses the flood plains and follows mule tracks ascending into the high rocky cliffs above the valley. Along the way, we cross the river and gradually climb toward the Toubkal Refuge (3,206 m ), following a steady path that snakes and zigzags up to the snowline.

Here, we spend the night in the Toubkal Refuge dormitories , surrounded by breathtaking mountain scenery. Dinner is served at the refuge, providing a chance to rest and prepare for the summit climb the next day.

itinerary.title: Mount Toubkal – Marrakech
body: Early in the morning, we begin our summit attempt of Jebel Toubkal (4,167 m ), the highest peak in North Africa. Our route ascends the south cirque, crossing the stream above the Toubkal Refuge. While the walk is relatively straightforward, the scree and high altitude make certain sections challenging, rewarding you with an unforgettable sense of achievement.

Upon reaching the summit, you’ll be treated to breathtaking panoramic views . Look north to the High Atlas, south to the Anti-Atlas and the Sahara, and across the Marrakech Plain—all visible from this commanding vantage point.
After soaking in the views, we descend the same route, returning to Imlil . From there, we transfer back to Marrakech , arriving by the evening and concluding your 2-Day Toubkal Trek adventure.
Highlights:
- Summit the highest peak in North Africa
- Uninterrupted panoramic views across High Atlas, Anti-Atlas, and Sahara
- Experience traditional Berber culture in the villages along the trail

seo.title: 3 Days Mount Toubkal Trek | Toubkal Peaks Travel Tours

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Toubkal Refuge
body: The trek departs from Marrakech around 9:00 AM (seasonal variations apply) for an exhilarating 1.5-hour transfer south through the dramatic Mly Brahim gorges to the Berber town of Imlil (1,740 m ). Nestled in the upper foothills of the Western High Atlas Mountains, Imlil is a major trailhead, with mule paths branching off in all directions.

From Imlil, we trek approximately 8 km to the picturesque village of Sidi Chamharouch, set beside a waterfall and stream. The village’s pisé homes appear built one into another, creating a charming and unique atmosphere. Sidi Chamharouch is a place of pilgrimage for devout Muslims, home to a marabout shrine —a sacred site not accessible to non-Muslims and believed to originate from pre-Islamic religious traditions.

We pause for a field picnic with full views of the mighty Jbel Toubkal (4,167 m ), the highest peak in the Maghreb. After lunch, the trek continues up to the Toubkal Refuge, where dinner is served and you stay overnight in the refuge’s dormitory-style accommodation .

itinerary.title: Mount Toubkal
body: We begin early with breakfast before setting out around 6:00 AM for the climb to Jebel Toubkal (4,167 m ), the highest peak in the Maghreb. The climb is non-technical but steep, taking approximately 3 hours, and offers breathtaking panoramic views—the highlight of your trek.

The first recorded ascent of Toubkal was made in 1923 by French mountaineers V. Berger, M. Doubleau, and the Marquis de Segonzac, and the mountain has since attracted countless trekkers seeking this highly rewarding experience.

After enjoying the summit views, we descend via the Ikkhibi Sud / South Cirque , a straightforward route with your guide, taking 2–3 hours back toward the Toubkal Refuge . Here, we enjoy a picnic lunch , followed by a gentle hike down in the afternoon.
The day concludes with dinner and overnight accommodation at the refuge, giving you a chance to rest and reflect on your remarkable achievement.

itinerary.title: Toubkal Refuge – Marrakech
body: After breakfast , we set off north along steep, zigzagging trails descending from the higher slopes of the Assif n’Isougan n’Ouagounss Valley toward the Berber village of Sidi Chamharouch (3,106 m ).

Before entering the village, your guide will show you a sacred tree , adorned with colored cloth strips and stones—a traditional site of significance for the local Berber communities. After a brief stop to relax, particularly welcome on a warm day, we continue the descent high above the Assif Aït Mizane Valley, winding down granite and basalt grey rocks for approximately 8 km to reach the fertile Berber village of Aroumd (Aremd, 1,840 m ), surrounded by terraced fields of maize, onions, and fruit trees.

We pause for a picnic lunch , before taking a well-defined mule track that zigzags along the valley floor for 4 km, arriving at Imlil around 1–2 PM. Here, enjoy a welcome glass of traditional mint tea at the home of our senior guide. Following this, we transfer back to Marrakech , arriving around 4 PM and concluding your unforgettable trek through the High Atlas Mountains.

tours.title: 3 Days Toubkal Experience

seo.title: 3 Days Toubkal Experience | Toubkal Peaks Travel Tours

summary: Embark on a rewarding 3-Day Toubkal Experience, designed to take you to the summit of Jebel Toubkal (4,167 m), the highest peak in North Africa, at a relaxed pace. This itinerary combines challenging mountain trekking with immersive cultural experiences in traditional Berber villages, allowing time to acclimatize, enjoy panoramic views, and experience the stunning landscapes of the High Atlas Mountains.
If you are trekking in winter (November to April), you will need crampons and an ice axe for safety on icy and snowy sections of the trail.

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Imlil – Azib Tamssoult
body: - Distance: ~10–12 km
- Elevation gain: +750m
- Elevation loss: –300m
- Highest point: Tizi n’Mzik Pass (2,489m)
After breakfast, you will be picked up from your Riad/Hotel in Marrakech at 9:00 am.
Your driver will transfer you to the trek starting point (Imlil, 1,750m), about 1.5 hours south of Marrakech.

Here, you will meet your English-speaking guide and muleteers. Once the mules are loaded, your trek begins with a steady climb out of the Imlil Valley, ascending to the Tizi n’Mzik Pass (2,489m), which rewards you with panoramic mountain views.

Stop en route for a picnic lunch with refreshing mint tea. Afterward, descend into the beautiful Azzaden Valley, known locally as the Valley of Colors. Continue toward Azib n’Tansoult, a small summer Berber goatherd village.
Overnight stay at the Azib Tamsoult Refuge (or camp, depending on weather conditions).

itinerary.title: Azib Tamssoult – Aguelzim Pass – Toubkal Refuge
body: Guide | Mule | Breakfast | Lunch | Dinner | 5–6 hrs Hike
- Distance: ~10–11 km
- Elevation gain: +1,350m
- Elevation loss: –350m
- Highest point: Aguelzim Pass (3,560m)

Early morning (around 6:00 am), after breakfast, you will begin a challenging but rewarding climb out of the peaceful Azzaden Valley. The day starts with a steep ascent, and very soon you will find yourself surrounded by rugged landscapes and ever-expanding views of the High Atlas.

A highlight of the morning is a stop by the Irhoulidene Waterfalls, cascading down from the cliffs above, where you can rest briefly and refill your water bottles. From here, the path winds its way upwards through alpine terrain, with fewer trees and more rocky landscapes as you gain height.

The climb continues until you reach the Aguelzim Pass (3,560m), the highest point of today’s trek. From the top, you are rewarded with breathtaking panoramic views over the surrounding valleys and the jagged ridgelines of the Atlas Mountains. On a clear day, you may even catch your first glimpse of Mount Toubkal rising above the horizon.
Lunch will be served at Agnierighen, a stunning viewpoint with wide-open vistas—an ideal place to rest, recover, and take in the silence of the mountains.

After lunch, the trail descends steadily toward the Toubkal Refuge (Neltner Hut, 3,207m). This mountain hut is the main base camp for climbers attempting Mount Toubkal. The atmosphere here is lively, with trekkers from around the world preparing for their summit push.

Settle into the shared dormitories and enjoy a warm dinner prepared by your support team. The evening will be spent relaxing, exchanging stories with fellow adventurers, and preparing for tomorrow’s exciting summit attempt.

itinerary.title: Toubkal Refuge – Mt Toubkal Summit (4,167m) – Imlil then Marrakech
itinerary.accommodation: Not included (return to your Riad/Hotel in Marrakech)
body: - Distance: ~18–20 km
- Elevation gain: +960m
- Elevation loss: –2,420m
- Highest point: Mount Toubkal Summit (4,167m)

Very early morning (around 4:30–5:00 am), you will begin the ascent of Mount Toubkal (4,167m), the highest peak in North Africa. The climb is steady but demanding, with rocky terrain and switchbacks as you rise above the surrounding ridges.

After 3–4 hours of trekking, you will reach the summit of Toubkal, where—weather permitting—you will be rewarded with unforgettable views stretching across the Atlas Mountains, the distant Sahara Desert, and the volcanic peak of Jbel Sirwa in the Anti-Atlas range. The summit experience is a moment of achievement, offering a chance to rest, take photos, and soak in the majesty of the High Atlas.
From the top, you will retrace your steps back down to the Toubkal Refuge (3,207m), where you will enjoy a short break before continuing your descent.

On the way down toward Imlil, you will pass the shrine of Sidi Chamharouch, a sacred site visited by pilgrims. Known locally as the “King of the Jinn,” this white-painted shrine is a fascinating glimpse into Morocco’s spiritual traditions.
The trail then winds down into the Imlil Valley, where your trek concludes.
From Imlil, you will be transferred back to Marrakech, arriving by early evening—tired but with a great sense of accomplishment.
End of trekking adventure.

body: - Morning hike: Depart Ouaougmout, walking through barley fields, almond groves, and pastoral valleys. Visit Tiziane village, where women bake bread in communal ovens.
- Scenery: Rugged hills, juniper trees, and red-earth terraces; classic Atlas panorama.
- Distance: ~14 km / 8.7 miles | Elevation gain: +250 m | Hiking time: 5 hrs
- Lunch: Picnic in Assaka village under walnut trees; enjoy quiet rural life.
- Afternoon: Continue to Tizgui n’Tkente (1,900 m), perched on a hillside. Sunset views over the valleys.
- Evening: Overnight in a Berber guesthouse. Dinner with hosts, opportunity to listen to traditional Berber songs by the fireplace.

itinerary.title: Tizgui → Azib Assoul → Tizi N’Tagdalt → Tizi Oussem
body: - Morning trek: Pass alpine meadows and summer pastures (Azib Assoul, 2,000 m), where shepherds graze their flocks.
- Climb: Ascend to Tizi N’Tagdalt Pass (2,700 m), the trek’s highest point. Panoramic views of the Azzaden Valley and surrounding ridges.
- Lunch: Picnic near the pass, surrounded by mountains.
- Afternoon descent: Into Azzaden Valley, lined with walnut groves, terraces, and stone villages.
- Evening: Overnight in Tizi Oussem (1,850 m). Dinner: vegetable tagine with local ingredients. Optional evening stroll in the village.
- Distance: ~12 km / 7.5 miles | Elevation gain: +450 m | Descent: -850 m | Hiking time: 5–6 hrs

itinerary.title: Tizi Oussem → Azib Tamsoult → Cascade Ighouliden → Refuge Lepiney
body: - Morning hike: Optional 2-hr trek to Azib Tamsoult (2,250 m) and Ighouliden Waterfalls. Stunning scenery, rivers, and mountain flora.
- Lunch: Picnic at Azib Berdoun (1,850 m), surrounded by forests and streams.
- Afternoon: Continue ascent along alpine trails to Refuge Lepiney (2,500 m). Observe snow-capped peaks, rock formations, and high-altitude vegetation.
- Evening: Overnight at Refuge Lepiney. Dinner: local ingredients, hot Berber meal. Prepare for summit climb.
- Distance: ~10 km / 6.2 miles | Elevation gain: +650 m | Hiking time: 5–6 hrs

itinerary.title: Refuge Lepiney → Tizi Aglzim → Refuge Toubkal
body: - Morning trek: Climb gradually to Tizi Aglzim Pass (2,900 m). Alpine terrain with panoramic views of Mount Toubkal and surrounding peaks.
- Lunch: Picnic along the trail with views of the High Atlas.
- Afternoon: Continue ascent to Refuge Toubkal (3,200 m), the base for the summit attempt. Optional exploration around the refuge.
- Evening: Overnight at Refuge Toubkal. Dinner: hot Berber meal, prepare for early summit.
- Distance: ~10 km / 6.2 miles | Elevation gain: +700 m | Hiking time: 5–6 hrs

itinerary.title: Mount Toubkal → Imlil → Marrakech
body: - Early morning ascent: Reach Mount Toubkal summit (4,167 m) at sunrise. Panoramic views of the High Atlas, Berber villages, and valleys below.
- Descent: Return to Refuge Toubkal for breakfast, then continue down to Imlil (1,740 m).
- Lunch: Picnic or at a Berber family home in Imlil.
- Afternoon transfer: Imlil → Marrakech (~1.5 hrs).
- End of trek: Arrive in Marrakech early evening.
- Distance: ~14 km / 8.7 miles | Elevation gain: +967 m | Descent: -2,427 m | Hiking time: 7–8 hrs

tours.title: 6-Days Mt Toubkal & Sahara Desert Adventure

seo.title: 6-Days Mt Toubkal & Sahara Desert Adventure | Toubkal Peaks Travel Tours

itinerary.title: Marrakech → Imlil → Toubkal Refuge
body: We depart Marrakech around 9:00 AM, winding through the stunning Mouly Brahim gorges, where terraced fields, small streams, and traditional Berber villages create a picturesque landscape. Along the way, enjoy the contrast of red-earth mountains, olive groves, and river valleys that mark the High Atlas foothills.

Arriving in Imlil (1750 m), the main trekking hub, you’ll see mule caravans, small guesthouses, and the bustle of local markets. The trek begins from here, following a scenic path 8 km up to Sidi Chamharouch (2315 m). This village, set beside a waterfall and stream, is a spiritual site with a Marabout shrine, historically significant and restricted to non-Muslims.

Stop for a picnic lunch while taking in views of Jbel Toubkal (4167 m), North Africa’s highest peak. The trail continues to Toubkal Refuge (3207 m), nestled among rugged peaks and alpine meadows. Dinner and overnight are in dormitory-style accommodation, with the mountain air and evening silence providing a serene setting.
Highlights: Scenic trekking, waterfalls, panoramic mountain views, introduction to Berber culture.

itinerary.title: Summit Mount Toubkal
body: After an early 6:00 AM breakfast, the ascent to Mount Toubkal (4167 m) begins. The climb is steep but non-technical, passing alpine meadows, rocky ridges, and sparse shrubs adapted to high elevations. Trekking through this dramatic landscape, you’ll witness the play of light across the valleys and peaks.
The summit offers 360° panoramic views, including neighboring peaks, deep valleys, and terraced villages far below. It’s a moment for reflection and photography—the reward for your effort.

Descend via Ikkhibi Sud (South Cirque), a straightforward but scenic route, taking 2–3 hours back to the Refuge. Lunch is served with a backdrop of mountains and glaciers. The afternoon allows time for rest, light hiking, or photography, soaking in the alpine ambiance.
Highlights: Summit of North Africa’s highest peak, alpine flora, panoramic vistas, mountain culture.

itinerary.title: Toubkal Refuge → Imlil
body: Descend north along Assif n’Isougan n’Ouagounss Valley, observing terraced fields, riverbeds, and small Berber farms. Return to Sidi Chamharouch (2315 m), where a sacred Berber tree, decorated with colored cloths and stones, reflects ancient local customs.
Continue the descent to Aroumd (Aremd, 1850 m), a fertile valley surrounded by maize, onion, and fruit-tree terraces. The path follows zigzagging trails, with stops for photography and picnic lunch.

Arrive in Aroumd early afternoon; spend your free time exploring the village, visiting local markets, or relaxing at a traditional Berber lodge. This immersive experience offers a glimpse into daily Berber life and customs.
Highlights: Sacred Berber sites, fertile valleys, traditional agriculture, cultural immersion.

itinerary.title: Atlas Mountains → Dades Gorge
body: Depart Aroumd/Imlil at 8:00 AM, crossing the Tizi-n-Tichka Pass (2260 m), where mountains display red, gold, and grey strata, dotted with small Berber villages and kasbahs. Enjoy photo stops and short walks along the pass.

Visit Ait Benhaddou, a UNESCO World Heritage site, famous for its mudbrick Kasbahs and cinematic history (Gladiator, Lawrence of Arabia). Climb to the hilltop for panoramic views of the ksar and surrounding desert plains.

Continue through Skoura Palm Grove, Valley of Roses, and the unusual rock formations of Tamnalt Hills, before arriving at Dades Gorge. Overnight in a traditional Moroccan-style hotel amidst towering red and mauve cliffs.
Highlights: UNESCO heritage, cinematic landscapes, palm groves, rose valley, dramatic gorges.

itinerary.title: Dades Gorge → Merzouga Sahara Desert
body: Explore Todra Gorge, with 300 m-high cliffs rising above the river, favored by climbers. Continue through Berber villages toward Erfoud, stopping for lunch and interaction with locals.

Arrive at Erg Chebbi dunes, the gateway to the Sahara Desert. Enjoy traditional mint tea, then embark on a sunset camel trek to the desert camp oasis. Dinner is served under the stars in a nomadic-style tent, accompanied by Berber music, creating an unforgettable desert experience.
Highlights: Towering dunes, camel trekking, desert sunset, stargazing, Saharan culture.

itinerary.title: Sahara Desert → Marrakech
body: After sunrise over the Sahara, ride camels back to the hotel for breakfast and a quick shower. Begin the scenic journey back to Marrakech, passing Ouarzazate and the High Atlas Mountains.
Stop along the way for photography and to admire the changing landscapes—from desert dunes to palm oases, rose valleys, and rugged mountain peaks. Arrival in Marrakech is expected around 7:00 PM.
Highlights: Sunrise in the Sahara, panoramic High Atlas views, desert-to-city journey.
End of Adventure

tours.title: 7 Days Berber Heartland & Toubkal Summit Trek

seo.title: 7 Days Berber Heartland & Toubkal Summit Trek | Toubkal Peaks Travel Tours

summary: This incredible 7-day adventure is a cultural and trekking journey into the Berber heartland of Morocco’s High Atlas Mountains.

From remote valleys and traditional villages to the breathtaking Lake Ifni and the mighty Toubkal summit, you’ll cross high mountain passes, meet welcoming Berber families, and discover the raw beauty of Morocco.

itinerary.title: Marrakech – Imlil – Tizi n’Tamatert – Tacheddirt
body: After breakfast in Marrakech, you’ll be picked up by private transport and driven south into the foothills of the High Atlas (approx. 1h30).

Your trek begins in Imlil (1,740m), a bustling trailhead village. From here, you climb steadily up through terraced fields and juniper forests to the Tizi n’Tamatert Pass (2,279m), offering magnificent views of the Imnan and Imlil valleys.
You descend gently into the valley before arriving at Tacheddirt (2,300m), the highest permanently inhabited Berber village in the Atlas.
- Overnight: Berber guesthouse in Tacheddirt
- Meals: Lunch & Dinner included

itinerary.title: Tacheddirt – Tizi n’Likemt – Azib Tinzar
body: A demanding but rewarding day. You begin with a long ascent towards the Tizi n’Likemt Pass (3,555m), one of the highest passes in the Toubkal range.
The trail zigzags up a barren, rocky slope, but the views from the top are breathtaking — jagged summits, vast valleys, and on a clear day, even glimpses towards the Anti-Atlas.
From the pass, you descend into a beautiful high valley dotted with shepherds’ huts and summer pastures, finally reaching Azib Tinzar (2,300m).
- Overnight: Tent camp or shepherd hut (rustic conditions)
- Meals: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

itinerary.title: Azib Tinzar – Tizi n’Ouraï – Amsouzart
body: Today’s trail leads through wide alpine meadows before a steady climb to Tizi n’Ouraï (3,120m). This pass offers splendid panoramas across the valleys below and the snow-dusted peaks above.
The descent takes you through walnut groves, terraced fields, and traditional Berber villages until you reach Amsouzart (1,740m), a lively village with stone houses nestled against the mountainside.
Here, you’ll experience warm Berber hospitality in a family guesthouse.
- Overnight: Berber guesthouse in Amsouzart
- Meals: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

itinerary.title: Amsouzart – Lake Ifni
body: A shorter, more relaxed stage. You hike out of Amsouzart, passing through small villages and cultivated fields, before climbing towards the spectacular Lake Ifni (2,295m).
Surrounded by rocky peaks, this turquoise glacial lake is one of the most beautiful natural sights in the Atlas.
The afternoon is free to relax by the lakeshore, swim (in summer), or simply enjoy the peaceful atmosphere.
- Hike: 4–5 hrs | +600m
- Overnight: Lakeside camping under the stars
- Meals: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

itinerary.title: Lake Ifni – Toubkal Refuge
body: A tough but unforgettable day. From Lake Ifni, you climb steeply to the Tizi n’Ouanoums Pass (3,670m) — a dramatic col squeezed between towering rock walls.
The descent brings you into the heart of the Toubkal Massif, reaching the Refuge du Toubkal (3,207m) in the afternoon. This is your base for the summit attempt.
- Overnight: Toubkal Refuge (shared dorms)
- Meals: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

itinerary.title: Ascent of Mount Toubkal (4,167m)
body: The big day! An early pre-dawn start to climb North Africa’s highest peak.

The trail climbs steeply on rocky ground, gradually opening up to a wide ridge. After 3–4 hours, you’ll stand at the summit of Mount Toubkal (4,167m). The view is breathtaking — across the Atlas range, the Anti-Atlas, and on a clear day, even the Sahara stretching endlessly to the south.
After photos and celebration, descend carefully back to the refuge. Afternoon at leisure to rest.
- Overnight: Toubkal Refuge
- Meals: Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner

itinerary.title: Refuge – Imlil – Marrakech
body: Your final day begins with a long descent through the valley of Sidi Chamharouch, famous for its white rock shrine visited by pilgrims.
Continue down to Imlil, where your driver will be waiting for the transfer back to Marrakech. Arrival in the city by late afternoon.
- Hike: 4–5 hrs | -1,470m
- Drive: 1h30 to Marrakech
- Meals: Breakfast, Lunch
